articles.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost their [almost?] franchise quarterback, Baker Mayfield, to a thumb dislocation injury in their Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.With everybody losing hope of winning further games, Kenneth Gainwell is keeping it steady for everyone. The 27-year-old running back shared head coach Todd Bowles’ motivating message via USA TODAY:“The message definitely has been: we have to continue to do the small things. We have to continue to be a group that wants to go out there and win. Not guys that are just happy to play football on Sunday. But a group of people that want to come out here and win and like being together, man.”Despite keeping his team steady in the absence of their star QB, running back Kenneth Gainwell is being linked to other teams in a unique trade scenario. According to Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers could trade Kenneth Gainwell to the Minnesota Vikings or Miami Dolphins for a 2027 sixth-round pick.Buccaneers RB Kenneth Gainwell linked to Dolphins and VikingsKenneth Gainwell has not been utilized in Zac Robinson’s offense. He has just played 42 percent of the offensive snaps and recorded just 16 touches so far into the 2026 season.Back in 2025, he recorded 537 rushing yards on 114 carries with 5 rushing touchdowns, alongside 486 receiving yards on 73 receptions with 3 receiving touchdowns. In totality, 1,023 scrimmage yards and 8 touchdowns. This dual-threat running back is not being utilized by Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive coordinator Zac Robinson.As per Aug. 2026 Pewter Report, Gainwell has not been utilized as much as a running back.Instead, Zac Robinson is using Gainwell as a quick, easy throwing option for short passes near the line of scrimmage rather than handing him the ball to run. This gives Bucky Irving more chances to run the ball and perform as the primary runner.The offense has also put both running backs on the field at the same time to utilize both players’ strengths, using the 21 personnel formation.Now, this makes him an RB2 in Tampa Bay. When a dual-threat running back is not getting utilized to his full potential, one that is already double [wide receiver ability], then that player could be best suited for some other NFL team, definitely requiring some receiving corps help!For instance - Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings, as suggested by Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox. Now, why those? Let’s find out.Minnesota and Miami both have injured rostersThe Miami Dolphins urgently need running back depth as they lost their starter, De’Von Achane, to a season-ending knee injury suffered in a Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.Jaylen Wright is currently managing a foot injury as well as a stinger. He did not play in Week 3. He is being viewed as day-to-day. His availability is uncertain for Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings. Ollie Gordon II may be expected to take up the primary role, but he is too dealing with minor physical ailments.As per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, “Gordon and Wright will share the load in the short term, and Wright is expected to return from injury this week. One of the two could emerge over the next few weeks, but for now Miami plans to use both. Wright has big-play potential, while Gordon projects as more of an every-down back.”The Dolphins have two backs on the practice squad: Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington Jr. It would make immense sense to rely on an elite all-purpose weapon like Kenneth Gainwell.As for the Minnesota Vikings? Their veteran starter, Aaron Jones Sr., is playing through a knee injury, and primary backup Jordan Mason is on injured reserve with a fractured thumb until at least Week 7. The Vikings signed RB Devin Neal on Tuesday, but he ran for just 206 yards on 57 carries as a rookie New Orleans Saint last year.Depending on a reliable player like Kenneth Gainwell, who had a remarkable report card last season, would suit Minnesota’s dream of revamping itself.The Vikings could be looking to rebuild after losing QB J.J. articles.body: Gia Duddy is giving fans a glimpse into the less glamorous side of being an NFL WAG, but her latest complaint about life in Cincinnati did not resonate with fans. The social media influencer, who previously dated Tennessee Titans quarterback Will Levis, shared a video where she was ranting about being left behind in Cincinnati while her boyfriend prepares to travel with the Bengals. The video sparked a wide reaction amongst fans on social media, with some fans relating (rarely a few) to her frustration while others questioned the way she presented the situation.Gia Duddy’s ‘hard life’ as a Bengals WAG sparks ‘pick-me’ backlash from fansDuddy is seen talking about how lonely it is when suddenly everyone leaves because of the team and matches. “B*tch, I’m in Cincinnati, Ohio. You’re going to Miami? Bring me with you,” Duddy said in the clip.Duddy is currently dating wide receiver Andrei Iosivas, she also posted footage from Bengals training camp that included Iosivas catching a pass. She was also seen with a friends-and-family wristband to support him.The latest video adds another chapter to the NFL WAG storyline surrounding Duddy, who first became a familiar face to football fans during her relationship with Levis.Fans call Gia Duddy a ‘pick-me’ over WAG complaintsWhile some viewers saw Duddy’s video as a lighthearted look at the realities of dating an NFL player, others were far less sympathetic. Some social media users accused the influencer of leaning too heavily into her WAG identity, with some calling her a “pick-me” for publicly complaining about being left behind while her boyfriend travels with the Bengals. The criticism was less about the fact that she wanted to accompany her boyfriend and more about the way the situation was presented online.This isn't the first time Duddy has incorporated the NFL into her social-media content. Her relationship with Levis made her a recognizable figure during the 2023 NFL Draft, when cameras repeatedly captured her reactions as the quarterback waited to hear his name called. Duddy and Levis later split in 2023 after dating for several years.More recently, she has been seen around the Bengals and has shared content that fans interpreted as clues about her current relationship. articles.title: Doctor says Josh Allen has "0% chance" of missing the Patriots game after practice video
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen appears to be moving well just days after a knee scare raised questions about his status heading into Week 4.
articles.body: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen appears to be moving well just days after a knee scare raised questions about his status heading into Week 4. Allen was spotted participating in practice Wednesday, with NFL reporter Matthew Bové confirming his presence on the field. The sight of the star quarterback back at practice comes after Allen took a shot to his left knee during Sunday’s 24-16 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.Josh Allen spotted practicing after scary knee hit as Bills QB provides major injury updateAllen appeared to favor the knee after taking the hit late in the game, but the quarterback remained in the contest and helped the Bills secure the victory. Now, video from Wednesday’s practice appears to offer a more positive update.Bové posted footage of Allen at practice and simply confirmed: “Yes, he’s practicing.”The quarterback was seen walking around the field with no obvious signs of discomfort. The quarterback took a hit to the knee late in the game and appeared to favor the leg afterward, briefly raising concern about his status. Allen nevertheless remained in the game and finished Buffalo’s 24-16 victory. The injury became a talking point after the game as footage showed Allen appearing to limp, but the Bills did not indicate that he was in danger of missing the next matchup.Doctor reacts to Josh Allen’s practice appearanceSports medicine physician Dr. Jesse Morse also reacted to the footage, noting that Allen appeared to be moving well.“As expected, looks good,” Morse wrote.“Doesn’t seem to be favoring that left knee, which he took a shot on later in Week 3’s game.”Morse added that he believed there was “a 0% chance” Allen was going to miss the game, although he raised a question about whether the knee could have an effect on some of Allen’s play-calling or decision-making.That assessment is Morse’s personal medical commentary and not an official injury designation from the Bills.Allen’s return to practice is certainly a notable development after the quarterback appeared to be dealing with discomfort following Sunday’s hit. The Bills have not indicated that Allen is in danger of missing their upcoming game against the New England Patriots, and his participation Wednesday provides another encouraging sign.Still, the quarterback’s practice workload throughout the week will be worth monitoring as Buffalo prepares for the Patriots. For now, though, the biggest takeaway from Wednesday is simple: Josh Allen is practicing, and he does not appear to be favoring the knee that caused concern just days ago.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jaxson Dart Injury, Return Timeline Updated by Giants' John Harbaugh After QB's Knee Surgery
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday that Jaxson Dart's surgery for the damaged meniscus and MCL in his left knee "went well" but tempered any expectations about a potential playoff return.
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday that Jaxson Dart's surgery for the damaged meniscus and MCL in his left knee "went well" but tempered any expectations about a potential playoff return.

"Maybe that's a little ambitious," he noted.

When it was first announced that Dart would require surgery, Harbaugh seemingly left open the possibility of a playoff return should the Giants qualify.

"I think I said it. I said it. Regular season," he told reporters last week about how long Dart was expected to be out. "Other than that, how do you know? It depends on the recovery. You can't pinpoint it."

"I think he's determined. He's bummed. It's hard," Harbaugh added of Dart. "The season is not over, but it is for him. We kind of talked about that [in the team meeting], too. That was part of it. That was part of the deal. With injuries, there is a certain mourning that takes place. Had the same thing for Calvin [Austin]. Same thing over the years because you realize how hard it is for a player really. But it's tough on the team. It's tough on all of us."

His replacement, Jameis Winston, has struggled in relief duty, throwing for 229 yards, no touchdowns and an interception in parts of two games, completing just 51 percent of his passes while taking five sacks.

The Giants did add some insurance at the position on Monday, however, landing former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings. If the Giants are going to make the postseason, either Winston or McCarthy is going to have to lead the charge. And even then, don't expect to see Dart back on the field come January.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill drops a major clue on his next team with one cryptic ‘cold weather’ message
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill has once again sent NFL fans into speculation mode.
articles.body: Tyreek Hill has once again sent NFL fans into speculation mode. The free-agent wide receiver took to X on Wednesday and posted a short but intriguing message: “I think I’m ready for some cold weather.”The post came just days after Hill suggested that he was getting closer to returning to football, writing that it was “almost time to get off the couch and get to work.” Hill’s latest message immediately raised questions about where he could potentially continue his NFL career, particularly after a major development involving the Green Bay Packers.Tyreek Hill’s ‘cold weather’ post comes at intriguing timeHill spent the previous four seasons with the Miami Dolphins, a warm-weather environment, before being released in February. The 32-year-old receiver has been working his way back from the serious knee injury he suffered last season and has recently increased the hints that he could be preparing for an NFL comeback.His “cold weather” comment therefore caught the attention of NFL fans, who quickly began trying to figure out whether the post could contain a clue about his next destination.And one team immediately stood out.Packers connection emerges after Jayden Reed injuryHill’s post arrived on the same day the Packers announced that wide receiver Jayden Reed will miss the remainder of the 2026 season because of a neck injury that requires surgery.Green Bay placed Reed on injured reserve after the receiver suffered the injury during the Packers’ Week 2 matchup against the New York Jets. Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed that Reed will undergo surgery and miss the rest of the season, although the injury is not believed to be career-ending.But again, there is no confirmation that Hill was referring to Green Bay.The Packers connection is largely based on timing and circumstance. Green Bay has suddenly lost one of its key receivers for the season, while Hill is signaling that he may be nearing a return and has now publicly expressed an apparent willingness to play in a colder climate.Other cold-weather teams have also been mentioned in the speculation, including the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Baltimore Ravens. Hill also has an established connection to Kansas City, where he spent the first six seasons of his career before joining Miami.The bigger takeaway from Hill’s post may simply be that the veteran receiver appears increasingly focused on getting back onto an NFL field. articles.title: “I have been cheated on”: Joe Burrow’s girlfriend Olivia Ponton reveals painful dating history
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow likes to keep his love life quiet. His girlfriend, model Olivia Ponton, does not have the same rule.
articles.body: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow likes to keep his love life quiet. His girlfriend, model Olivia Ponton, does not have the same rule. She has a famous boyfriend, a big modeling career, and millions of followers. But on her Booked & Busy podcast, she admitted something many people hide: every partner before Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow cheated on her. Read that again. Every. Single. One. Ponton did not name any exes or share details.Joe Burrow's model girlfriend Olivia Ponton reveals cheating history on Booked & Busy podcast"I have been cheated on in all of my past relationships. Literally every single one of them," Ponton said.She said she used to "beat herself up" over it when she was younger. She believed she was not good enough, or that she had done something wrong.That is the part that hits. Cheating is one person's choice. Yet the person who gets cheated on often ends up on trial in their own head. What did I miss? Was I too much? Not enough? Ponton says she went through that loop. So do many women, models or not.Her answer now is simple. She called cheating "a sign of insecurity." In her view, someone who has a happy, healthy partner and still goes looking for outside validation is showing their own problem, not their partner's flaw."That's my hot take," she said.Burrow and Ponton have been linked since 2024. Two years later, they are still together. The couple has been spotted out and about this year, including events in March and during practices. Ponton also stepped out this week for the premiere of Amazon MGM Studios' Verity in New York City.Expect some people online to read this as a message to Burrow, or as proof he is the "good guy" boyfriend. Do not buy either one. Ponton spoke only about her past relationships. She did not mention Burrow in the parts that have been reported.What we can say: Burrow's girlfriend is comfortable sharing her dating history in public, and Burrow, who avoids the spotlight, has a partner who does the opposite. Burrow is one of the biggest names in the NFL, so anything about his girlfriend gets attention. Add a "cheating" headline, and it spreads fast. But so far there is no drama here. articles.title: Gervon Dexter, Falcons Agree to Contract Extension After Trade from Bears, Details Revealed
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $78 million with defensive tackle Gervon Dexter on Wednesday, agents Drew and Jason Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $78 million with defensive tackle Gervon Dexter on Wednesday, agents Drew and Jason Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter .

The deal includes $46.5 million guaranteed, per Schefter.

Dexter is in the midst of his first season with the Falcons after they acquired him from the Chicago Bears in exchange for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a fifth-round draft pick on Aug. 30.

Dexter has been a key starter on an Atlanta defensive front that ranks No. 3 among all teams with a 61 percent pass-rush win rate, via ESPN .

In three games this season, the 24-year-old has amassed seven tackles, three quarterback hits, one pass defended and 0.5 sacks. He's also racked up 14 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus .

Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham discussed the new extension.

"Gervon is a young, ascending talent whose power, disruption and impact along the defensive line are difficult to find," Cunningham said Wednesday, per Tori McElhaney of the team's official website. "What's been just as impressive is the growth he's shown off the field as a man and a father. His passion for the game and commitment to his teammates are qualities we value highly, and we're excited to keep him as an important part of our defense moving forward."

Dexter was initially selected by the Bears with a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, operating in a rotational role as a rookie before becoming a full-time starter during his sophomore season in 2024.

He finished with 45 quarterback hits and 14 sacks across 49 total games throughout his tenure in Chicago.

Now, Dexter's long-term future in Atlanta is secure as the team looks to improve upon a 1-2 start to the 2026 season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $1.7 billion baseball venture hits major milestone just months after ownership move
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has another reason to celebrate away from the NFL field.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has another reason to celebrate away from the NFL field. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end is now part of the Cleveland Guardians’ ownership group, and his first season with the franchise has already brought a memorable moment. Cleveland clinched the American League Central title, securing another trip to October baseball. For Kelce, the achievement means more than a successful season. The Guardians represent his hometown, while baseball has been part of his life since childhood. His latest connection to the sport brings an old passion back into focus.Travis Kelce celebrates Cleveland Guardians’ division titleThe Cleveland Guardians punched their ticket to the MLB postseason on September 26 after beating the Kansas City Royals 11-5. The victory secured their third consecutive American League Central crown and marked another strong regular-season run under manager Stephen Vogt.Kelce did not wait long to celebrate. After the Guardians sealed the division, the NFL star took to Instagram Stories and shared a message with fans.“October baseball baby!! LFG Guards!!!” Kelce wrote on Instagram Stories.The Guardians also earned the American League’s No. 2 seed, which means they will receive a first-round bye. Cleveland is set to host Game 1 of the American League Division Series at Progressive Field on October 3 against the winner of the Astros and White Sox series.Kelce became a minority owner of the Guardians in May 2026. The investment added a new chapter to his connection with Cleveland, where he grew up before becoming one of the NFL’s biggest stars.Travis Kelce’s baseball connection goes back yearsLong before Kelce became a Super Bowl champion and NFL star, baseball was a serious part of his sporting life. His father, Ed Kelce, coached him from T-ball through youth baseball, and Kelce continued playing multiple sports at Cleveland Heights High School.His baseball ability was especially noticeable during his senior year in 2008. Kelce reportedly hit .588, prompting high school coach Michael Dillon to draw a bold comparison.“He would have been an Aaron Judge-type player,” Dillon said.Baseball also remained in Kelce’s thoughts during his college career. After a suspension kept him away from Cincinnati’s football team during the 2010 season, he played summer collegiate baseball and considered whether the sport could become another path.“I could track a baseball in the outfield,” Kelce said in 2024. “Like, I felt like I would always get a chance. So it was always in the back of my mind that I had that as a plan B, which is why I tried to, you know, play in 2010 when I got kicked out of school or when I got kicked off the team for a little bit. I was always just kinda keeping that alive in a sense.”Football ultimately became Kelce’s calling. Yet his investment in the Guardians shows that baseball never completely left his story. articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders faced renewed scrutiny after a former member described low pay, strict appearance rules, mental health struggles and
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders faced renewed scrutiny after a former member described low pay, strict appearance rules, mental health struggles and safety concerns behind the famous team. Speaking anonymously to Daily Mail Sport, the former cheerleader said the strong bond between members often helped them cope with the pressure. She said the job gave them close friendships but also left some feeling underpaid and replaceable. The Netflix documentary America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brought several of these issues to a wider audience. Since then, the team has also announced a major pay increase.Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders pay and strict rulesThe former cheerleader said she earned between $15,000 and $22,000 a year during her time with the DCC and needed two other jobs to cover her expenses. She also questioned comments from Charlotte Jones, who said in the Netflix series that dancers were drawn by passion, purpose and sisterhood rather than money.“It’s very insulting to see someone in such a high position talk about the fact we’re in it for something bigger than ourselves,” the former cheerleader said.“We love the job of being a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader. However, I believe if you want elite dancers, you have to give elite compensation.“We’re all athletes, we’re all incredible performers … the problem is that they will have women lining up every single year willing to do it for less.”The issue had already led to legal action. Former DCC member Erica Wilkins sued the Cowboys over pay in 2018. A 2019 settlement increased hourly pay from $8 to $12 and doubled the game-day payment from $200 to $400.The situation changed again in 2025. Season two of the Netflix series revealed that the cheerleaders received an approximately 400% pay increase. The exact new rates were not publicly disclosed.The former member also described pressure around appearance and strict rules. She said the team expected dancers to maintain a certain image and that mental health support was difficult to afford.“I didn’t have body image issues until I became a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader, and I also didn’t have a lot of the bad habits I have now until I was a DCC: I’m a severe people pleaser and overthinker to the max, I’m constantly worried that people are upset with me, even if I’m doing a good job at my work or in relationships.”Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders safety concerns and the Netflix seriesSafety was another concern shown in America’s Sweethearts. Senior member Kelcey Wetterberg spoke about finding an AirTag on her car and the fear it caused her. Another storyline involved Sophy Laufer, who reported that a cameraman had grabbed her after a Thanksgiving game. Police did not bring charges because authorities said there was not enough evidence.The former cheerleader said the pressure could be difficult to leave behind.“You kill your body for years and years for this job where you make nothing. Then at the end of the day, you are viewed as expendable and they will replace you so fast.”She added that the bond between members was still important.“You get hooked on the sisterhood of it all,” the former cheerleader said. “You really fall in love with the girls, they’re your best friends. articles.title: Sean McVay says NFL has admitted officials made major mistake that probably cost the Rams a loss vs Denver
articles.summary: Sometimes NFL officials get it wrong. Sean McVay says the league admitted the pass interference penalty on Josh Wallace was not the right call.
articles.body: Sometimes NFL officials get it right. Sometimes they get it wrong. And when that happens, the NFL often acknowledges the mistake to its teams, as it did with the Los Angeles Rams and their controversial pass interference call against the Denver Broncos. The NFL has apparently admitted its officials were wrong to call pass interference on Rams defensive back Josh Wallace in the Sunday Night Football game. NFL'S MOST DEBATED WEEK 3 CALL HAS PEOPLE WONDERING HOW TO DEFY GRAVITY WHEN HITTING PATRICK MAHOMES That call almost certainly cost the Rams the game. Rams coach Sean McVay said Wednesday he was told by the league that Wallace should not have been called for defensive pass interference on that play. Huge if true. The NFL did not immediately respond to an email from OutKick seeking confirmation that the league acknowledged the officiating mistake to McVay. So we're going on his word only. But the coach has no reason to lie. The penalty against Wallace was a double whammy. It negated what would have been a potential game-sealing interception with 1:09 remaining to play and the Rams leading 26-23. The blown call instead resulted in pass interference against Wallace and the Rams. That gave the Broncos a first-and-goal situation at the Los Angeles 7-yard line, setting up a touchdown six plays later and a 30-26 Broncos win. It should be noted that Wallace did indeed make contact with Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant. But in a league that often prefers to let players decide games in the final minutes rather than having officials determine the outcome, referee Bill Vinovich's crew stepped in, and they pretty much helped decide the game. Regardless of the mistake, the NFL is not awarding the Rams anything other than maybe some satisfaction. The Rams still carry the loss in the standings and the Broncos keep their victory. Kudos to the NFL for admitting its officials were wrong, especially since league officials had to know that telling McVay would be as if broadcasting it nationwide. He wasn't going to treat that communication as a secret. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And while we're discussing Vinovich's crew and the mistake, we all have to give NBC officiating guru Terry McAulay respect. Immediately after the controversial call, McAulay was asked to chime in on the broadcast and told everyone what he saw. There was no interference. He disagreed with the officials. Big ups to McAulay for getting it right even if it meant disagreeing with his former officiating brethren. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Now the starter, QB Jalon Daniels is staying cool in the spotlight
articles.summary: Jalon Daniels knows the Packers will try to dial up the heat and apply pressure Sunday when he makes his first NFL start at quarterback. But the kid known fo...
articles.body:
Jalon Daniels knows the Packers will try to dial up the heat and apply pressure Sunday when he makes his first NFL start at quarterback. But the kid known for his cool under pressure isn't going to take the temperature about how he feels heading into his pro debut.

"I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," said Daniels, an undrafted rookie. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it."

The Bucs originally planned for former Bengals quarterback Jake Browning to be the backup to starter Baker Mayfield . But Daniels outplayed him, and head coach Todd Bowles made the risky decision to make the former Kansas star No. 2.

"He earned it and he beat him out fair and square," Bowles said.

The Bucs have had remarkable luck in terms of continuity at quarterback. The last starter to miss a game for any reason was Jameis Winston , when he was suspended the first three games of the 2018 season for violating the league's personal conduct policy. But Winston was replaced by veteran Ryan Fitzpatrick .

Daniels played well in the preseason, leading comeback wins over the Jets and Chiefs. Mayfield hadn't missed a start in 54 games before suffering a dislocated thumb in Sunday's loss to the Vikings, which dropped the Bucs to 0-3.

So Daniels' job isn't just to keep the season afloat, he has to prevent it from sinking it completely before Mayfield returns. Daniels believes he's up for the challenge.

"I may not have been getting those reps, but as I've told you every single week, I prepare as if I'm going to go out there and get the starting reps. So whenever Bake is throwing to them, I'm behind him doing every single step that I can," Daniels said. "And when it comes to footwork, just standing behind and trying to be able to be on time just like Bake is. Obviously, I had a chance to be able to get reps with those guys (Wednesday) and I think it was a great start to the week."

In Sunday's 23-16 loss, Mayfield was sacked six times, putting him at 13 for the season, the most in the NFL. Daniels knows that the Packers will try to dial up pressure on him early and often.

Like Mayfield, Daniels has the ability to escape the pocket and either throw off-platform or make some plays with his feet. He rushed for 1,445 yards and 23 touchdowns with the Jayhawks.

"When the defense is locking everything up, sometimes you have to be able to get out of the pocket and try to be able to go make plays," Daniels said. "Because at the end of the day, at the quarterback position, your objective is to try to be able to move the chains on every play. … I try to get out of the pocket and find a receiver downfield. And if I can't find a receiver downfield, the objective is to be able to move the sticks.

"That's been part of my game since I've been playing football when I was 7 or 8 years old."

Daniels' teammates don't believe that starting against Green Bay , and likely four days later in Dallas , will be too big for him. He appeared in 49 games over parts of six seasons for the Jayhawks.

"He's played a lot of football in his life," Bowles said. "It's not about playing twice in 10 days. I think he's done that in college some and he's played against our defense from a pressure standpoint every day in the summer. There will just be all eyes on him as opposed to not on him.

"He's a very calm customer. He'll be comfortable very soon in the game and we just expect him to do his job and everybody else has got to do theirs."

Daniels has been underestimated for much of his career. Growing up in California, he took a backseat to Bryce Young , Jayden Daniels and D.J. Uiagalelei even though Jalon had led his high school to a state title in 2018.

On Sunday, he will become the first NFL rookie to start at quarterback this season.

"I don't even know if I can put it into words," he said. "I mean, obviously I've said it's a dream come true to even play for an NFL organization. So to be able to go out there and have my first NFL career start, it means everything."

articles.title: Inspiring story on marriage:“Our marriage is a partnership, we are equals who are figuring it out on the daily"- How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce built a family rooted in love and partnership
articles.summary: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce have built a marriage that often stands out for a simple reason: neither appears to treat family life as one person’s
articles.body: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce have built a marriage that often stands out for a simple reason: neither appears to treat family life as one person’s responsibility. Their approach came into sharper focus when Jason addressed criticism over Kylie’s role at home, explaining that their marriage works through shared effort rather than fixed expectations. Behind the NFL fame, packed schedules and public attention, the couple has created a family structure based on communication, flexibility and mutual support. Their story offers a relatable look at how two people can divide responsibilities while keeping the same goal at the centre: building a home together.Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce see marriage as a partnershipJason Kelce’s comments about his marriage came during a wider conversation about the role of homemakers and expectations placed on women. His response was notable because he did not describe Kylie’s contribution through a traditional label. Instead, he focused on the way the couple works together.“I don’t think of Kylie as a homemaker,” Jason replied, adding: “Our marriage is a partnership, we are equals who are figuring it out on the daily. The only expectation is that we love each other, support one another, and are committed to our family, that comes first. We both raise our kids, we both work, we both keep our home. It is both our faults it is messy, but such is life with 3 young children.”That explanation gives an insight into the way Jason views family responsibilities. The point was not that Kylie does not handle household duties. Instead, he described those duties as part of a wider arrangement that belongs to both partners.Their lives have also required flexibility. Jason spent years dealing with the demands of an NFL career, including travel, training, games and recovery. Kylie has taken on a major role in managing family life while also pursuing her own interests and work.Rather than presenting those responsibilities as permanent job descriptions, Jason described them as something the couple works out together.That distinction is important. A family’s needs can change. So can careers, schedules, finances and personal priorities. A partnership has to leave room for those changes.Kylie Kelce’s role goes far beyond the label of homemakerKylie Kelce has often been associated with her role as a mother and wife, but her life includes much more than the work that happens inside the Kelce home.She has participated in community and advocacy work and has also developed her own public platform. Her identity is not limited to being Jason Kelce’s wife or the mother of their children.At home, however, raising children naturally requires a large amount of time and organisation. Child care, appointments, schedules, meals and everyday household decisions do not always appear in public, but they can shape the rhythm of family life.Jason has openly acknowledged his own involvement as a parent. In the documentary Kelce, one scene showed him caring for one of his young children while dealing with his own physical discomfort. The moment offered a more ordinary picture of life away from the football field.That kind of involvement matters because parenting is rarely about one dramatic gesture. It is built through repeated small tasks.Someone gets the child ready. Someone handles dinner. Someone manages an appointment. Someone stays awake when a child needs comfort. Sometimes the same person does more, and sometimes the balance shifts.For Jason and Kylie, the idea of partnership appears to come from recognising that both people contribute to the family, even when those contributions do not look identical.Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce put family before public expectationsBeing part of a famous family can create pressure to maintain a certain image. Jason and Kylie Kelce have instead spoken about family life in a way that feels grounded in everyday realities.Jason’s response to criticism showed that he does not believe a marriage should be defined by outsiders deciding what each partner ought to do. He described the couple as equals who continue to figure things out together.That approach also allows the family to adapt.Jason’s NFL career required a level of commitment that few ordinary jobs demand. His schedule could involve long days away from home and extensive travel during the season. Kylie therefore had to manage many aspects of family life around that reality.But an unequal amount of one type of work does not necessarily mean one partner has less value. A household involves many forms of labour, including financial support, child care, emotional support, planning and maintaining a home.The key issue is how couples decide to share those responsibilities.Jason and Kylie’s comments suggest that they do not see marriage as a competition over who contributes more. Instead, they appear to approach it as a shared project.That perspective can become particularly important when raising children. Their daughters are growing up in a household where both parents have demanding responsibilities, but where family remains the central priority.The Kelces’ marriage shows why flexibility mattersOne of the most relatable parts of Jason’s comments was his admission that their home can be messy.“It is both our faults it is messy, but such is life with 3 young children.”The line may sound lighthearted, but it captures something many parents understand. Family life does not always look polished. A busy home with young children creates noise, clutter, rushed mornings and unexpected problems.The pressure to maintain a perfect household can make ordinary family challenges feel like failures. Jason’s comment offered a different perspective. A messy home can simply mean that people are busy living in it.That attitude also connects with the couple’s broader approach to responsibility. They appear to recognise that family life cannot always follow a fixed plan.A schedule that works one year may not work the next. A career change can alter the balance. Children grow and develop different needs. Personal goals can change too.A strong partnership therefore requires more than dividing tasks once and leaving them there. It requires regular conversations about what the family needs.For Jason and Kylie, that seems to be part of what keeps their relationship grounded.Their marriage has also developed in the public eye, where every comment can attract attention. Yet the principles Jason described are not particularly complicated. Love, support, commitment and shared responsibility form the foundation.Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s family-first approachJason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s love story goes beyond being an NFL star and his wife balancing family life. Their relationship reflects how two people can build a family while managing demanding careers, parenthood and constant public attention.Jason’s comments shed light on how he views their partnership. He does not believe Kylie’s role in the family is defined by traditional gender expectations. Instead, he sees their responsibilities as part of an arrangement they have created together.That does not necessarily mean everything is split equally at all times. Family life can shift depending on circumstances, with one partner sometimes taking on more responsibilities while the other steps up when needed.For the Kelces, recognising each other’s efforts and respecting what each person brings to the family appears to be central to their relationship. Their approach suggests that partnership is less about dividing every task equally and more about supporting each other when circumstances change.Their marriage also highlights that equality does not require both partners to have identical roles. Different contributions can have equal value when both people appreciate the work involved and remain willing to share the responsibility.Away from the NFL, cameras and celebrity headlines, Jason and Kylie’s relationship reflects a more relatable side of family life. articles.title: Saints work out 7 free agent running backs and edge rushers
articles.summary: Seven more free agents worked out for the New Orleans Saints, with multiple running backs, defensive ends, and a linebacker in the mix.
articles.body:
Seven free agents worked out for the New Orleans Saints on Wednesday, with a mix of different positions in the group. Among those seven, three were running backs, three were defensive ends, and one was a linebacker. This depicts a somewhat obvious trend; with Travis Etienne Jr. , Anfernee Jennings , and Pete Werner all suffering injuries this past week, depth will come at a premium for those positions.

So let's take a quick look at each free agent who tried out in New Orleans . With multiple players having tried out at different positions on Tuesday already , this is now the second wave of options. These were the three running backs in for a workout on Wednesday:

Ulysses Bentley IV , Ole Miss . Bentley IV, 25, was an undrafted free agent signing back in 2025 for the Indianapolis Colts , and would spend time on and off their practice squad as a fringe player, signing a futures contract for 2026 but being removed once again before the season. He spent six years at the NCAA level, three with SMU and three with Ole Miss, the best of which was 2020 when he had 170 rushing attempts for 913 yards and 11 touchdowns.

Hassan Haskins , Michigan. Haskins, 26, was previously a fourth-round selection in 2022 by the Tennessee Titans , spending two seasons there, two with the Los Angeles Chargers , and then a short stint on the practice squad with the New England Patriots this year. He has predominantly been used as a short-yardage back; in 44 games played, he has 76 rush attempts for 229 yards and 2 touchdowns, and 23 first downs. He also works a bit in the receiving game, posting 18 receptions for 119 yards and a touchdown.

Elijah Mitchell , Louisiana. Mitchell, 28, was a sixth-round selection by the San Francisco 49ers back in 2021, and has by far the most NFL experience of the bunch. Injuries have haunted him over the past few years, with an MCL tear and a season-ending hamstring injury in 2022 and 2024, respectively. However, his 2021 season looms large, when he had 207 rushes for 963 yards and 5 touchdowns, along with 19 receptions for 137 yards and a touchdown. While he has mostly been a practice squad player since 2024, he may still have something left in the tank.

Here's a look at the three defensive ends:

Vincent Anthony Jr., Duke. Anthony Jr., 22, is one of the youngest players brought in over these two days by the Saints, as a 2026 undrafted free agent signing from the Kansas City Chiefs . He also was on the practice squad for the San Francisco 49ers, but was cut on Tuesday, so the Saints looked immediately to see what he's got. His 2025 season at Duke was a strong one, posting 7.5 sacks, 34 total tackles, 13 tackles for loss, 2 pass deflections, and a forced fumble.

David Ojabo , Michigan. Ojabo, 26, is one of the players with more draft pedigree to his name of the bunch, as a former second-round selection by the Baltimore Ravens in 2022. Unfortunately, a torn Achilles at his pro day stunted his initial development in the NFL, and then an ACL injury in 2023 slowed it even further. After four years with the Ravens, he had 4.5 sacks and 2 tackles for loss to his name, signing to the Miami Dolphins ' practice squad for 2026. He ended up being cut during final roster cutdowns, but could be an interesting option if he can remain healthy and work in a strong defensive scheme.

Julian Okwara , Notre Dame. Okwara, 28, has played a pretty decent clip in the NFL, as a third-round selection back in 2020 by the Detroit Lions . He has spent time with four different teams since then, including the Philadelphia Eagles , Arizona Cardinals , and Cleveland Browns . In 51 career games, he has 10 sacks, 15 tackles for loss, 72 total tackles, 4 pass deflections, an interception, a forced fumble with the recovery, and 31 total pressures.

And finally, here is the one linebacker who worked out amongst this group:

Jesse Luketa , Penn State. Luketa, 27, was a seventh-round selection in the 2022 NFL Draft by the Arizona Cardinals , but was also selected in the 2022 CFL Draft in the second round. He stuck with the Cardinals for three seasons, playing in 31 games and starting three, putting up 3 sacks in his 2024 campaign. Ultimately, he has been on the Los Angeles Rams and New England Patriots practice squads since then, but has not made it back to an NFL roster yet.

The Saints have not signed anyone just yet, but stay tuned. They're visibly looking into bringing in quality depth on defense and at the running back position.

articles.title: What I’m hearing at Gillette Stadium: Wednesday word (Week 4)
articles.summary: The preparation for the Week 4 matchup against the Bills is officially underway for the Patriots.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass — There was lots to talk about at Gillette Stadium on Wednesday, with potential drama between the head coach and the quarterback as well as cryptic answers about a shoulder injury. And all of that was answered.

Plus, the focus has now shifted to the Buffalo Bills as the New England Patriots are looking to turn things around following a 1-2 start.

Here's what I heard at Gillette Stadium on Wednesday:

For the past few days, Drake Maye has been evasive about a potential shoulder injury. And the reason for that has been discovered.

Following pracice, he was asked a simple yes or no question about his shoulder and if that's impacted his throwing.

"No, it hasn't. I don't think it impacts my decision-making, and that's what makes and breaks play for quarterbacks," he said. "I don't feel like we're struggling to move the ball. I think we're turning the football over, doing things that are preventing us from scoring touchdowns, and I think that's one of the biggest things for me. I think we've had a history of good football when we don't turn the football over, playing good football and finding ourselves on the right side of games. So, that's the biggest thing, and I'm looking forward to another good week of practice. I felt good out there today.

But shortly after, the quarterback made his debut on the injury report with a shoulder injury, but was listed as a full participant.

Mike Vrabel, Drake Maye addresses viral WEEI report

On Wednesday morning, WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" made waves with a report of a potential rift between Vrabel and Maye.

"Wiggy and I were whispered to about this," Hill said. "On this very show yesterday, we talked about being whispered to about an issue between the head coach and the quarterback. … If you believe this individual, who is an insider. I mean, he's very much an insider. Despite what Mike Vrabel may have said publicly, it goes back to Drake Maye not being his guy."

However, when asked about this, Vrabel didn't mince words.

"He heard from who? Unnamed sources? Let me just tell you why I'm here. I'm here because Drake was the quarterback," he stated. "Believe it or not, I had choices as to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here because Drake was the quarterback. So, I don't have really much other to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source. But I'll just tell you what I've told numerous people if they want to ask me why I'm here."

"Coach Vrabel's been one of the best football coaches I've had in my life," the quarterback said. "I think Coach Vrabel's been one of the biggest things as to why this has been so enjoyable for me is playing for Coach. I think we all feel that way in the locker room. He pushes us hard. I've loved playing for him, and it's not going to change. It hasn't changed, and it won't change. The way he pushes me, and he coaches the quarterbacks in a way that I really respect, and I'm looking forward to getting going, proving to Coach that I can lead this football team and play good football."

Three players were absent from Wednesday's practice, all of whom are key starters. Cornerback Christian Gonzalez and defensive tackle Christian Barmore were both out with shoulder injuries, while offensive tackle Morgan Moses was sidelined with a foot injury.

As for linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee), outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder), tight end Eli Raridon (thigh), safety Brenden Schooler (back), and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder), they were all listed as limited. And then there's Maye, who was a full participant while dealing with a shoulder injury.

With Greg Van Roten now being placed on injured reserve, the Patriots have lost their top backup at right guard. On Sunday, it was Walter Rouse who subbed in, but he struggled immensely. So, what's the plan for this week?

"Walter and Ben [Brown] will work in there today and tomorrow, and we'll kind of see where that goes for the week," Vrabel said.

Vrabel was also asked if there was any consideration of moving starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker to the right side as well.

"Again, the vision that I have for AVT and Will [Campbell], you're starting to see a little bit of that," he added. "And I want to continue that, so probably not right now."

Preparing for Joe Brady and the Buffalo Bills

After losing in an embarrassing fashion to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, things aren't going to get any easier for the Patriots as they now have to go up aaginst the tough Buffalo Bills team that is firing on all cylinders.

"They're really successful in a lot of things they do," Vrabel said. "They rarely punt: five punts in three games. Josh does a fantastic job of being able to extend plays. The linemen do a fantastic job of understanding the scheme that they want to run and creating lanes for [James] Cook, who again, once he gets cooking – no pun intended, but they're just tough to stop, right? Because then it's play action, it's boots. And so, it just makes it tough to stop. [Dalton] Kincaid has been fantastic lately, averaging almost 19 yards a catch. The quarterback's tough to bring down. But I think the line is a very underrated part of what they do. It's been a very consistent unit, one that knows how to block for not only the running back, but also for the quarterback."

Maye also shined a light on the Bills' defense.

"I think it's the guys they've had," the quarterback said. "I've played them for a couple of years now. [Terrel] Bernard in the middle and [Greg] Rousseau on the edge, and they've got some new additions. But these guys are Bills players. They're in the right spot. They're coached well. They know tendencies. They know what we like to do, and I think one of the best things about what they do is they're going to make you earn it. I think that's the Bills, and we've got a tough challenge. So, I'm looking forward to getting back up there, seeing the new stadium. They know who they have on offense and how explosive their offense is. So, they do a nice job of making you earn it and making you drive the football."

The Patriots' run game has struggled to start the season, and they know they need to improve if they want to get back on track and back in the win column.

"It's not good enough, honestly," Rhamondre Stevenson told Patriots Wire. "But it's early in the season, just something you've got to get comfortable with. Just me, the O-Line, and Trey, just running behind our pads and getting on the right track."

The Patriots have brought in another offensive tackle, signing Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad. He entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent, signing with the Bills. But he was released by Buffalo at the end of training camp.

Mike Vrabel says the two open roster spots "are not filled" as of Wednesday, but the team did sign someone to the practice squad.

Mike Vrabel on Harold Landry 's possible return: "Correct. Not yet. Harold continues to work hard to try to get back. I think we'll just have to be smart about when we start his window and then what that looks like. But not yet."

After Kevin Byard III said on NBC Sports Boston's Early edition that the team had a 45-minute meeting regarding the bad plays and holding others accountable, Vrabel was asked about it and said, "We don't want to be the issue. We want to be the answer." He added that this is "a great opportunity for us to be the answer, to understand that we choose our demeanor, we choose our attitude, we choose our response. That's not up to anybody else."

articles.title: Should the Cardinals bring in a seasoned cornerback?
articles.summary: There is trouble brewing in the defensive secondary
articles.body:
During training camp, there were several Arizona Cardinals cornerbacks who were on the mend from various injuries and ailments. But the consensus was that this position group was on the verge of being one of the league's finest.

Which was a huge requirement. Because Arizona resides in the most difficult division in the NFL, the NFC West, the defensive backfield is expected to be battle-tested each and every week. Great quarterbacks and even better receivers dot each roster in the division.

Will Johnson has shown that he can become one of the best cornerbacks in the division as well as in the league. Last year, Denzel Burke , proved his worth when he was thrust into the starting lineup; the experience of Garrett Williams was apparent, and Max Melton had games where he showed he belonged, although his play is more summed up as a roller coaster.

However, in the Week 2 matchup against division foe Seattle Seahawks , Johnson suffered a neck injury in the loss and later was added to IR. It now looks like he could be gone for the remainder of the season. Which is a huge, huge loss to this defensive backfield.

Burke has filled in for Johnson while Melton has been added to the starting lineup with Williams in the slot. Starling Thomas was brought up from the practice squad, and the team is now dependent on Kei'Trel Clark and Kalen King as key backups.

But this cornerback group has shown anything but consistency in being able to stop an opposing offense's passing attack. You might even say this group is in trouble.

Part of the reason is not only the loss of Johnson, who was this defense's best cornerback, but also having to shuffle guys around into different positions. Plus, it is a very young room. Williams has the most games played, with 36 NFL games and 27 starts. But all of the other corners have minimal game experience.

Another issue is that the defensive front four is not getting a good pass rush, which means opposing quarterbacks are being given ample time to survey the field and wait for guys to complete their routes. The inability of the defensive line to collapse the pocket makes it harder for the cover guys to continue to shadow their guy, and opposing receivers have been open all day long in all three games.

Not to mention, a guy like Burke should have been brought along gradually after being taken in the fifth round in last year's NFL Draft. Instead, he was thrust into the starting lineup last year, which has carried over into 2026. In the above clip, Burke bit on the early wiggle by WR Mike Evans , but had the speed to catch up. However, he never even looked back at the ball. If he had looked back when Evans did, Burke could have swatted the ball away and possibly intercepted the pass. Instead, it was six for San Fran, which was the difference on the scoreboard at the final gun.

After just three games, the Cardinals are allowing more yardage through the air with each contest. In Week 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers , QB Justin Herbert threw for 209 yards with a single touchdown and one interception by safety Andrew Wingard . Against the Seahawks, the backup quarterback, Drew Lock , threw for 235 yards and tossed three touchdowns against zero interceptions. After a 7-7 halftime score, Lock found receivers open all day long in the second half. In this past weekend's division matchup against the San Francisco 49ers , QB Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards, connected on four touchdowns, again with zero interceptions.

That equates to seven touchdowns through the air in two straight games without any picks. Is anyone paying attention?

This season will be over very soon if this is not addressed. Opposing quarterbacks are being given way too much time without a valid pass rush, and the defensive backs are not able to keep running with receivers who can change their routes, wave their arms, and be wide-ass open.

So, what is the answer? Keep doing what they're doing and expecting Burke, Williams, and Melton to take care of business?

Or maybe sign a free agent? What about a trade? Johnson ain't coming back this year, which means their best cornerback is gone. If the Cardinals truly want to salvage this year, they have got to bring in a seasoned veteran.

Let's start with the trade angle first. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in a contract dispute with their starting cornerback, Joey Porter Jr. (6'-2", 193 pounds). He believes he is an elite corner and should be paid as such. Pittsburgh views him as just an above-average guy who hasn't even sniffed a Pro Bowl. Porter has yet to suit up for the Steelers this year, even though he has been completely healthy each week.

Porter was taken in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft and was named to the NFL "All-Rookie Team" after being a First Team All-Big 10 selection in his final year at Penn State. His father was an NFL player, so he's got pedigree. Pittsburgh signed Porter to a four–year, $9.61 million deal that included $8.99 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $3.99 million.

Which means Porter is in his contract year. He had 43 total tackles as a rookie, 70 in his second season, and 52 last year. He has 3 career tackles for loss, 0 QB hits, 1 sack, 31 batted passes, 3 interceptions, 1 hurry, 2 pressures, and 17 missed tackles.

Do any of these stats scream elite? What they do say is that Porter is an above-average cornerback who is aggressive, has speed, has no issue in the run-defense game, and is around the ball a lot, but his missed tackles are an issue.

If the price is right, it is assumed that the Steelers would be all ears. They don't believe he will suit up for them this year at all, period. He could step in that first week after arriving in the desert and take Johnson's place. As Pittsburgh is preparing to face their second straight divisional game against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football, Porter Jr. was listed as a full participant on the Steelers' injury report for the first time this season.

The trade issue may be that the Steelers view Porter Jr., age 26, as more valuable than his production has been so far as an NFL player. If their wish list is a first-or second-round pick for the disgruntled cornerback, then they may just have to keep him. But perhaps a third-round pick may entice them to allow him to leave.

As far as scouring the free agent market, the list has been picked over pretty well.

Trevon Diggs (6'-1", 203 pounds) leads the list. He is 29 years old so he has some years left in him. His last contract was for $19.4 million, but is currently on the Dallas Cowboys practice squad making $13,750 a week. Sean Murphy-Bunting (6'-0", 195 pounds), age 29, has seven years of experience and was paid $4.45 million in his last gig with the Cardinals. He is on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers practice squad. Kader Kohou (5'-10", 197 pounds) is the last of the top cornerback prospects who was paid $3.26 million. He currently resides on the practice squad of the Kansas City Chiefs .

All practice squad players are available to every NFL club at all times. With all three of these candidates, all the Cardinals have to do is make a roster claim and then add him to the 53-man roster (after dropping a player).

The current cornerback cast is struggling. Each game, the opposing QB increases his total passing yards and touchdown throws. The status quo is not an option.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's $200 million Six Flags investment faces new low as investors push for a potential sale
articles.summary: Six Flags is facing a fresh challenge after an investor group that includes Travis Kelce pushed the theme park company to consider a possible sale.
articles.body: Six Flags is facing a fresh challenge after an investor group that includes Travis Kelce pushed the theme park company to consider a possible sale. The move comes as the operator deals with heavier losses, fewer visitors and pressure on its stock price. Jana Partners, which joined Kelce and other investors in taking a stake in Six Flags, is now seeking action from the company’s board. The development marks a sharp turn from the group’s earlier effort to help strengthen the parks and improve their appeal to families.Six Flags faces mounting financial pressureJana Partners reportedly contacted Six Flags’ board on Tuesday and asked it to bring in an investment bank to examine a potential sale. The request followed disappointment over the company’s latest financial results, which showed how difficult the current environment has become for the theme park operator.Six Flags posted a $203 million net loss for the second quarter, more than double the $100 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier. Attendance also fell. The company reported 13.1 million guest visits, down about 7% from 14.2 million visits in the comparable period.The pressure has also reached the stock market. Six Flags shares traded at about $12.43 on Wednesday, roughly half their yearly peak of close to $25.Jana Partners and fellow investors, including Kelce, acquired a combined stake of around 9% in Six Flags last October. Their investment was valued at roughly $200 million at the time. Jana had previously focused on improving the company's marketing and customer experience while also considering strategic options that could increase shareholder value.Six Flags said it remains focused on its investors and its wider business plans."We have a history of engaging constructively with all of our shareholders and value their perspectives. We are focused on executing on our strategic priorities and are committed to maximizing shareholder value."Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment faces another testKelce's connection to Six Flags goes beyond his investment. The Kansas City Chiefs star has long had an attachment to Cedar Point in Ohio, a park he visited while growing up.When the investment was announced, Kelce shared his excitement about helping shape the company's future."Couldn't pass up the opportunity to continue the tradition and make Cedar Point and Six Flags even more special for the next generation of families!"He added, "Excited to partner with JANA Partners as an investor in Six Flags. So crazy to even imagine this is real, but you gotta love it when life comes full circle."The company is also dealing with legal challenges involving its X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California. Three people who say they suffered serious brain injuries after riding the attraction have filed lawsuits. The coaster, known for rotating seats and head-first drops, remains closed.Attorney Christopher Bulone said, "No ride like that should be allowed to exist," according to CNN.Six Flags declined to comment on the pending lawsuits but confirmed to KABC that the ride "remains closed at this time."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mike Tomlin Shows Off Minecraft City in New Video After Former Steelers HC's Viral Comments
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin showed off the city that he built in Minecraft on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin showed off the city that he built in Minecraft on Wednesday.

Tomlin provided a closer look at his first building downtown as well as other rooftop properties that he created in the game during a video posted on YouTube.

Tomlin's son, Mayce, also explained that his father would occasionally take his PlayStation to play the game.

Former Steelers running back Le'Veon Bell gave his thoughts on his old head coach's hobby as well.

On Sept. 8, Tomlin revealed that he had been constructing his Minecraft city for over a decade in an interview with TODAY 's Craig Melvin .

"I started playing Minecraft, man, when my kids were young," Tomlin told Melvin. "I have a Minecraft city, I'm creative, that I've been working on for like 12 years."

"We've been talking recently about sharing it with the world," he added. "My oldest son is like, 'Dad, you gotta share this with the world. People need to see this city that you've been working on for 12 years.' We've been talking about it recently about how am I gonna share it with the world."

The 54-year-old eventually teased the unveiling of his city in a Saturday post on X.

Tomlin previously spent 19 seasons patrolling the sidelines for the Steelers from 2007-25, as he was the NFL's longest-tenured head coach before he stepped down from the position on Jan. 13.

Pittsburgh went 193-114-2 under Tomlin, never posting a losing record in any year that he spent with the team. The Steelers made several playoff appearances over that span, capturing a Super Bowl title during their 2008 campaign.

Tomlin currently serves as an analyst for NBC Sports.

articles.title: Titans QB Cam Ward brushes off criticism, threats he and family have received after 0-3 start: 'People are weird'
articles.summary: Cam Ward's sister spoke out on social media after their loss to the Giants on Sunday.
articles.body:
Cam Ward is brushing off the threats that frustrated Tennessee Titans fans have been sending his family in the wake of their rough start to the season.

"I mean, at the end of the day, people are weird," he said on Wednesday, via ESPN .

The Titans have opened the season 0-3, and Ward has struggled at the start of his second campaign in the league. The former Miami standout and No. 1 draft pick most recently threw a bad interception late in their 12-7 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday. The Titans were right up against the goal line with just 24 seconds left in the game when Jevon Holland intercepted Ward, which sealed the loss.

Though the Titans' struggles aren't all on Ward, he's been taking the brunt of the criticism. Things have gotten so bad on social media that his sister even spoke out.

"The fact I even have to post this is diabolical," she wrote on an Instagram story on Sunday, via ESPN . "People see the football games, they see the wins, the losses, the interceptions, the touchdowns, the press conferences and everything that happens on the field. What they don't see is what comes with it for the people who love these players when the game is over. "Criticize the game, criticize a play, be frustrated with your team. That's sports, and I completely understand that. But seeking out a player's sister, parents or other family members to personally attack them because you're upset about what happened on a football field is something completely different."

"The fact I even have to post this is diabolical," she wrote on an Instagram story on Sunday, via ESPN . "People see the football games, they see the wins, the losses, the interceptions, the touchdowns, the press conferences and everything that happens on the field. What they don't see is what comes with it for the people who love these players when the game is over.

"Criticize the game, criticize a play, be frustrated with your team. That's sports, and I completely understand that. But seeking out a player's sister, parents or other family members to personally attack them because you're upset about what happened on a football field is something completely different."

Ward went 23 of 36 for 181 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the loss. He's thrown for 504 total yards and two touchdowns so far this season while completing better than 62% of his passes.

Ward and the Titans will next take on the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. A win there will end their losing streak and avoid matching last year's 0-4 start to the campaign.

As for the criticism and threats that he and his family are receiving, Ward knows there's one sure way to get it to stop.

"They can say whatever they want at the end of the day, but I think football will take care of a lot of it," he said. "My family knows the position I'm in and what I've wanted my whole life. They're in this position as well with me … Every adverse situation I have, I'm going to take on. It's really just about making plays on the football field. If I do that, we do that as a team, it's going to cut all that out."

articles.title: “He wants to be around you. He’s just not ready to talk”: How Kylie Kelce’s childhood bond inspired Jason Kelce’s autism mission while teaching their daughters about acceptance
articles.summary: Kylie Kelce’s connection to autism started long before she became Jason Kelce’s wife or a familiar face around the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body: Kylie Kelce’s connection to autism started long before she became Jason Kelce’s wife or a familiar face around the Philadelphia Eagles. It began with a childhood friendship that stayed with her into adulthood. Now, that same bond has shaped her family’s philanthropy and the way she and Jason teach their four daughters about autism, respect and acceptance.For Kylie, the lesson starts at home. Her daughters know the person who helped shape her understanding of autism, and she uses those everyday moments to help them understand that people can communicate and behave differently without changing how much they deserve to be loved.Kylie Kelce’s childhood friendship became the starting point for her and Jason Kelce's autism missionKylie Kelce grew up close to a neighbour named Tim, who is on the autism spectrum. Their friendship continued into adulthood, and Tim became an important part of Kylie’s family. Her daughters, Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finnley, now know him as “Uncle Tim.”Kylie explained the connection during an April 17, 2026 appearance on CBS Mornings, where she joined Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jihaad Campbell to discuss autism awareness.“Tim was my introduction to autism,” Kylie said in the Eagles Autism Challenge impact report, explaining that the connection stayed close to her heart and led her to take part in autism awareness work.Her relationship with Tim also helped Jason understand autism in a much more personal way. Before meeting Kylie, Jason said he had little connection to the autism community. Meeting Tim changed that.“The first time I met Tim, I knew that he was a big part of Kylie’s family,” Jason said in the Eagles Autism Challenge impact report. “I wanted to impress him and I wanted to make sure he liked me.”That personal connection eventually became part of the Kelces’ wider philanthropic work.Since 2021, Jason and Kylie have used Team 62 to raise money for the Eagles Autism Foundation. Their sixth annual fundraiser in Sea Isle City on June 24, 2026, raised a record $1.26 million. The six Team 62 fundraisers have now generated more than $3.69 million for autism research and care programmes.The Kelces’ work also goes beyond writing checks. The June 24, 2026 Team 62 event included an All Abilities clinic at Excursion Park, giving families a space built around activities for people of different abilities. The fundraiser also featured yoga, an online auction and the New Heights Beer Bowl. That mix of fundraising and inclusion reflects the wider work Kylie and Jason have backed through the Eagles Autism Foundation. Their four daughters are learning the same lesson through “Uncle Tim”The money raised tells only part of the story. Kylie has also brought the cause directly into her home.During her April 17 CBS Mornings appearance, she explained that she talks to her daughters about Tim in simple, everyday terms. She does not want them to see his differences as something frightening or strange.“We just talk about sort of his quirks,” Kylie said on CBS Mornings. She then explained what she tells the girls when Tim does not immediately respond to them: “He still loves you, and he wants to be around you, but maybe he’s just not ready to talk.”Kylie Kelce said she keeps those conversations “very matter of fact.” She wants her daughters to understand Tim as a person first, rather than reducing him to his diagnosis.That approach also fits the wider way Kylie and Jason Kelce talk about raising their children. In a March 25, 2026 appearance on Cameron Oaks Rogers’ podcast, Kylie said the couple wants their daughters to grow up grounded and learn to become “good people.”For Kylie, the lesson started across the street when she was a child. Years later, it has reached her four daughters, Jason’s understanding of autism and a philanthropic effort that has raised millions for the Eagles Autism Foundation. The family connection came first.
