articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Traded to Cowboys in New NFL Rumors Following Steelers Contract Standoff
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly moving on from starting cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after stalled extension negotiations.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are reportedly moving on from starting cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after stalled extension negotiations.

The Steelers traded Porter to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday, per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer. ESPN's Todd Archer provided details on the deal:

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

Despite the trade, the Cowboys don't plan to sign Porter to an extension immediately and will instead play out the year on his current deal, per NFL Insider Jordan Schultz .

Porter, who has not yet played this season, is under a $4.9 million cap hit in the final year of his rookie contract .

The Steelers attempted to finalize an extension for Porter this offseason but did not come to resolution before the franchise's Week 1 negotiating deadline, which general manager Omar Khan told reporters in August the franchise did not plan to change.

Porter was placed on the PUP list in early August after reportedly aggravating a back injury. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said later that month the team was at an "impasse" in contract negotiations with Porter.

The cornerback ultimately missed the first three games for the Steelers before he was traded without having played a snap in 2026.

The news comes after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the Cowboys had joined teams including the Detroit Lions in making inquiries about Porter.

The Cowboys ultimately won that potential bidding war as part of the team's ongoing effort to overhaul its defense.

Dallas started last season by acquiring Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams, then added Rashan Gary before drafting Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence last spring.

The Cowboys will now continue that effort by addressing the secondary, which struggled early this season after losing Cobie Durant to injury.

Dallas will hope adding more pass protection will help the team improve on a 1-2 start to the season.

Porter missed three games due to injuries last season, including two with a hamstring issue and one with a hip injury.

When available he recorded 52 tackles, 14 passes defensed, a sack and an interception while playing 94 percent of the Steelers' defensive snaps.

Those snaps were mostly run defense and coverage, per Pro Football Focus . Porter ranked top-five in the NFL in yards allowed per coverage snap last season, per PFSN .

Porter has not allowed a touchdown on a regular-season coverage snap since Week 8 of the 2023 season, per NFL Next Gen Stats cited by former NFL scout Matt Williamson .

His defensive efforts down the stretch were a key reason the Steelers made it into the playoffs before losing in the Wild Card round to the Houston Texans.

The Steelers responded to that playoff loss by bringing in McCarthy to replace longtime head coach Mike Tomlin this offseason.

McCarthy, who said in August he would like to coach Porter, will now hope to see his franchise make some more moves ahead of the deadline in order to bolster their secondary in Porter's absence.

articles.title: Steelers trading CB Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys after failed contract negotiations
articles.summary: Porter is in the final year of his rookie deal.
articles.body:
The Steelers are receiving a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round selection from the Cowboys , Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein confirmed .

After being selected with a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Porter is playing in the final year of his rookie deal, which will pay him $3.924 million. Porter and the Steelers were unable to reach a contract extension in the offseason.

Porter won't get an imminent extension in Dallas, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Porter hasn't asked for one yet either, the Dallas Morning News' Calvin Watkins reported .

Pittsburgh general manager Omar Khan had reiterated on Aug. 31 that the team does not deal with extensions during the season, and no deal was completed when the Steelers took on the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1.

Porter has not played this season and was ruled out of the Steelers' Thursday night game against the Browns. He has been listed with a back injury, but many believed his contract situation played a role in his missing the game. It's yet to be seen if he'll play for the Cowboys on Sunday.

Reports earlier in the day indicated that the Lions and Giants offered third-round picks for Porter , but no team had floated a second-rounder. Apparently that changed on Wednesday night.

Porter is the third Steelers player traded to the Cowboys in a 17-month span. In May 2025, the Cowboys acquired wide receiver George Pickens and a 2027 sixth-round pick for a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth. In August, the Cowboys sent a pair of 2027 draft picks (third and sixth) to Pittsburgh in exchange for tackle Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder.

The cornerback likely wanted to be paid like a top player at his position, but after Christian Gonzalez (four-year, $135 million) and Devon Witherspoon (four-year, $132 million) signed mega deals this offseason, Pittsburgh opted not to pursue a record-setting deal and made a trade.

Porter was drafted with the 32nd overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, which was technically the first pick of the second round. The Miami Dolphins had their pick forfeited after the league found them guilty of tampering.

As a rookie, Porter played in all 17 games, starting 11. The corner had 43 total tackles, 1 interception and 10 passes defended.

Over his three-year career, Porter has tallied 165 combined tackles, 3 interceptions and 31 passes defended. Last year, the corner played in 14 games and finished with 52 total tackles, one sack, one interception and 14 passes defended.

The cornerback is the son of former NFL player and Steelers star Joey Porter. He was a linebacker in the NFL from 1999 to 2011, splitting time between the Steelers, Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals . Over the course of his career, he tallied 689 total tackles with 12 interceptions in 188 games.

articles.title: Grade the trade: Cowboys get CB Joey Porter Jr. from Steelers
articles.summary: The Cowboys added an impact defensive player to help on that side of the ball.
articles.body:
Jerry Jones said before the season that he was itching to make another big trade .

The Dallas Cowboys owner made a move, with room to possibly make another splash before November's trade deadline. Dallas dealt a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for their young cornerback Joey Porter Jr., a second-round selection in 2023, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein . Netflix's Tom Pelissero initially reported the trade .

It wasn't the all-in move that Jones has teased. But it's still a big move that should help improve a defense that hasn't been great to start the 2026 season .

Here are the grades for the late Wednesday night trade:

Porter had started to become a distraction for the Steelers. He was seeking a contract extension, it didn't get done, and then he was sitting out games. A back injury was the official reason he hasn't played yet this regular season, but it was hard to believe that his absences weren't contract related.

The move continues to add to a Dallas defense that was horrible last season. The Cowboys made several offseason additions, including at coordinator with the hire of Christian Parker, though there hasn't been a big turnaround. The Cowboys have given up the third-most yards in the NFL this season. Their secondary has given up seven touchdowns with no interceptions. Of 99 qualified corners for Pro Football Focus' grades this season, no Cowboys cornerback ranks in the top 50. DaRon Bland is 55th, Cobie Durant is 67th and Shavon Revel is 85th. Durant is dealing with a hamstring injury that will likely keep him out of this week's game against the Houston Texans , and Revel didn't practice Wednesday with knee and ankle injuries.

Porter helps right away, assuming he can play soon. It will be costly over time. The second-round pick the Cowboys gave up is valuable, and Porter is going to want a big contract extension. He has a lot of leverage after the Cowboys gave up picks to get him. It's a fine move that helps a defense that needed a boost in a wide-open NFC East. But it wasn't cheap.

Pittsburgh wasn't as high on Porter as he was on himself because a contract extension never happened. ESPN's Dan Graziano suggested Porter wanted to be paid $30 million per season. Only six cornerbacks are making that per season.

Pittsburgh had an issue on its hands because Porter wasn't playing, and it seems like more than a coincidence that he hasn't played yet this season while he's also upset about his contract.

"My back has its moments where [there's] a flare up here and there, and we're still just trying to get my conditioning down to just me being out there as much as possible," Porter said this week .

Porter was a hit for the Steelers in the second round three years ago. He became a very good player, though perhaps not one worth the top of the pay scale at cornerback. His PFF grade last season ranked him 36th among cornerbacks — the best grade of his first three NFL seasons — and he has not been named to a Pro Bowl.

The Steelers used a second-rounder to get Porter and after three seasons they got a second-round pick back for him, while adding that sixth-rounder. They won't pay Porter a costly extension.

It's not fun to let go of a good homegrown starter, but it was also going to be hard for the Steelers to find a trade partner that would give up a second-round pick knowing Porter also is seeking a big extension. The Steelers pulled that off, and their Porter drama is over. It's not an ideal ending but it solves some issues.

articles.title: As Jerry Jones' 84th birthday nears, Cowboys' trade for Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is a fitting early birthday present
articles.summary: Dallas sits at 1-2 with a need to improve in several areas. But its offense is explosive, and the cost to acquire Porter shouldn't hurt their immediate windo...
articles.body:
Sometimes, Jerry Jones sticks to talking a big game.

Other times, the Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager puts his money — and draft capital — where his mouth is.

After Jones told reporters on Sept. 20 that "there's nothing more dangerous than an old man with money," the Cowboys have upgraded their secondary.

Schematically, first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker's case for hiring came in part on the basis of how he elevated the Philadelphia Eagles secondary in 2024 and 2025. His talent collection there included 2024 first-round cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and 2024 second-round safety Cooper DeJean .

The Cowboys showed a commitment to upgrading their secondary when they traded up to select safety Caleb Downs 11th overall in the spring. There was still need for more talent if Dallas' defense was going to survive while its high-powered offense thrived. Changing the Cowboys to a 3-4 base defense for the first time in 13 years was going to require some personnel adjustments.

Jones' looming 84th birthday, and the expiration of star receiver George Pickens ' contract this spring, were each reasons to lean into a 2026 contention window.

"We're right on top of it," Jerry Jones told Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday when asked about Porter. "We're very aware of the moving parts out here. We should be. And communication is a big part of it … communication at all levels. At my level, at Stephen's level, at the scouts' level. We all have contacts and this is a time where you really can have discussions and they could be productive.

"Yes, there are conversations going on."

Since the Steelers selected Porter in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, he's started 41 games, deflected 31 passes and intercepted three balls. Porter combined for 165 tackles and three tackles for loss in Pittsburgh.

He didn't play the first three weeks of this season after negotiations reached a point of contention, instead sidelined with what the injury report described as a back issue.

The Steelers ruled Porter out for Thursday night's game against the Cleveland Browns . He increasingly seemed available. And the Cowboys, whose Rio de Janeiro implosion against the Baltimore Ravens included a 27-yard completion in the final seven seconds of the game, increasingly needed help. Their starting core was light. Injuries had left their secondary still thinner.

And the NFC East appears wide open. The New York Giants , since beating the Cowboys in Week 1, have lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart and top pass rusher Brian Burns to season-ending injuries. The Philadelphia Eagles lost to a third-string quarterback on Monday night in Chicago . The Washington Commanders are 1-2 and dealing with an injury to QB Jayden Daniels .

Dallas sits at 1-2 with a need to improve in several areas. But its offense is explosive, and the cost to acquire Porter shouldn't hurt their immediate window. So a Cowboys team that spent several years quiet on the in-season trade market continued its trend of activity that began last year with a deadline acquisition of defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . A Cowboys team that's become familiar with Steelers decision-makers from recent trades for Pickens and left tackle Broderick Jones hit speed dial to run it back one more time.

On Oct. 13, Jones will turn 84. Wednesday night, as September became October for the Steelers and Cowboys, Jones gifted himself an early birthday present.

articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have witnessed a difficult start to the season despite entering the year with plenty of offseason hype, dropping to 1-2 following their Week 3 loss. With head coach Brian Schottenheimer preparing the Cowboys for their Week 4 matchup against the Houston Texans , the team has also made headlines by reportedly acquiring Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

NFL World Erupts After Steelers Trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys

Just three days before Wednesday's trade, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that several teams, including the Cowboys and Detroit Lions , had started exploring the possibility of acquiring Porter. He had been seeking a contract extension, but Pittsburgh has traditionally avoided negotiating new deals during the season.

Porter said last week that he would "definitely" play at some point this season, while also saying he had not requested a trade. The subsequent trade, however, changed that outcome.

According to Ari Meirov, Pittsburgh would receive a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for Porter.

Porter has yet to appear in a game this season as he continues to work his way back from a lingering back injury. He had been listed as a full participant in practice but was ruled out of Pittsburgh's Thursday night matchup with Cleveland because of his back issue before the trade was finalized.

Meanwhile, Porter's trade immediately drew reactions from across the NFL world.

"Joey Porter Jr's back injury just cleared right up!" Fantasy Points' injury analyst Jeff Muller wrote .

"Playoff Baseball rocks. But Joey Porter Jr. just got traded to the Cowboys… THAT'S CRAZY," ESPN's Sam Block wrote .

Dallas has been aggressive in reshaping its defense, acquiring Quinnen Williams , Rashan Gary , and Kenny Clark via trades while also using first-round picks on Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence.

Meanwhile, Porter gives Dallas another option at cornerback, an area where the Cowboys have dealt with inconsistency early in the 2026 season. If he can return to full health, his arrival could strengthen a Dallas secondary that has struggled for consistency early in the season.

From Pittsburgh's perspective, the emergence of Asante Samuel Jr . and Daylen Everette gives the Steelers additional options at cornerback following Porter's departure.

Meanwhile, some were clearly dissatisfied with the move.

"Steelers haven't learned. They keep getting fleeced by Dallas huh," one said .

Steelers Depot's Alex Kozora also questioned the move, writing : "The third trade between the Steelers and Cowboys the last two years. George Pickens , Broderick Jones , and now Joey Porter Jr. Crazy how we got here but felt like this was Pittsburgh's only move left. #Steelers."

"Why do we keep making the same mistakes?" Gutfoxx, a popular content creator and streamer, wrote .

Onyx Odds also joined the reaction with a meme depicting Cowboys fans asking Jerry Jones to improve the defense.

In Dallas, Porter joins a defense that has undergone significant changes over the past year. The Cowboys have added defensive linemen Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary, and Kenny Clark through trades, while first-round picks Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence have added young talent to the unit.

Porter now gives Dallas another option in the secondary as the Cowboys look to improve a defense that has struggled through the opening weeks of the season. It remains to be seen whether Porter's addition can change the fortunes of the Cowboys' defense, which now ranks No. 31 in PFN's Defense impact score with a 67.1 grade.

articles.title: What was learned from Dallas' Week 3 loss to the Ravens?
articles.summary: Poor coaching on offense and special teams execution cost the Cowboys a win in Week 3, where their young defense made enough plays to win.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys found a way to lose another game they could've won. They faced off with the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and went toe-to-toe down to the last second of the contest. The Ravens got the ball with seven seconds left after Dallas chose not to go for a touchdown on third-and-goal and also chose not to squib-kick the kickoff. Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers to set up a game-winning field goal for Baltimore.

This was a game dictated by poor decisions on offense and special teams, leaving the door open for the Ravens offense to take the win against a defense decimated by injuries in the defensive backfield. What was learned from the Cowboys' Week 3 contest is that the young defense is improving, but their offense, and especially the coaching staff's decision-making on that side of the ball, has to help win these games. The money is on the offensive side of the ball, so they have to pull wins out of games like this one.

Schottenheimer's play-calling hurt the Cowboys' quick start

Dallas didn't run the ball from the 1-yard line on second or third down . The offense rushed for over seven yards per attempt on the opening drive, with two rushes of eight yards and one of 17 yards. The first dynamic run of the season from anyone not named Dak Prescott . The two plays to get them to the 1-yard line were four-yard runs. Shottenheimer got too cute and called two pass plays, and the Cowboys had to kick a field goal.

On their third drive, up 10-7 on a second-and-six, Shottenheimer split the running back out wide while averaging 6.1 yards per attempt. At a time when the Dallas offense should be protecting its defense, Williams could've been used to run or for a play-action pass. Dallas threw the ball all four plays on that drive and ended up punting. The momentum shifted in favor of Baltimore mainly due to their head coach and play caller.

The offense had chances to put the game away and failed

With the team up 28-24, the defense got a three-and-out, making the Ravens punt the ball back to the Cowboys' offense with 7:29 left in the game. Asking them to milk seven minutes is a lot, but if they can drive down and score a touchdown, they go up two scores with less than five minutes left. Instead, Dallas went three-and-out, running two balls up the middle for a total of four yards and then throwing an incompletion.

After a Baltimore touchdown, Dallas drove down inside the five and couldn't punch it in to win the game. They threw a pass, took a false start penalty, had a QB scramble, and then inexplicably threw it away on third down. The defense was missing multiple defensive backs , so not going for the game-winning touchdown on third down was an awful decision. One long completion and a timeout later, and Dallas loses 34-31.

The Cowboys rookie class is making plays early in their careers

The Dallas defense played well enough to win. Were they still a bad defense overall? Yes, and they should still look to improve the roster on that side of the ball , but given the situation, the defense did enough, and the rookie class is a major part of that. They forced a three-and-out on the first defensive drive, but the Cowboys couldn't score a touchdown from the one-yard line. The defense then caused a turnover on downs when rookie Caleb Downs tackled Derek Henry in the backfield. The rookie class's first big play set up the offense for the early touchdown from the 30-yard line.

In the second half, Jaishawn Barham made two huge stops. One on third-and-one, where he got a tackle for a four-yard loss, and then a goal-to-go tackle of Henry, causing a turnover on downs. LT Overton made a big play at the goal line later, but Baltimore scored two plays after negating the impact of his play. That doesn't change the fact that the defensive rookies are making plays, and the more snaps they get, the better they should get. More experience, better instincts, less reaction to fatigue. The foundational pieces are there.

articles.title: ‘Jerry’s going for it’ – NFL fans react to Dallas Cowboys’ blockbuster Joey Porter Jr. trade
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have made a big win-now move by trading for Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have made a big win-now move by trading for Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The Dallas Cowboys have started the 2026-27 NFL season 1-2, but they have shown signs of promise. The team has what it takes to compete with the best in the league.

That doesn't mean they can't get better, and owner Jerry Jones is seeing to it that they do. The Cowboys have made a huge move late on Wednesday night.

Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been in a contract standoff with the team since the offseason. Dallas has swooped in to take advantage of the situation.

NFL fans think the Dallas Cowboys won the trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers

The Cowboys are reportedly sending the Steelers a 6th-round pick in 2027, and a 2nd-round pick in 2028 for the star cornerback.

After the news came out, fans on social media had a lot to say about it. For the most part, the consensus seems to be that Dallas has gotten a great deal.

"Jerry's going for it, this is just the sort of move we needed," one fan wrote on X. "Jerry I take it all back, this is amazing," another fan claimed.

"Oh my god Jerry's actually going all in," a third fan said. "Dallas has literally zero interceptions all year, so this is a no-brainer," a fourth fan observed.

"Wow! Actually shocked they did it. Now they gotta pay him too," read another comment. "I'm ready for the Cowboys to pay him whatever if he can help this defense out," a sixth fan wrote.

Porter Jr. has been dealing with a back injury to start the 2026 season. Apart from concerns over his health, this looks like it might be an excellent move by Jones and the Cowboys.

After three weeks of action in the NFL, there's been some clarity as to which fantasy football players are good and which are bad. With this information, let's look at which quarterbacks you should consider starting in Week 4 and which quarterback you should hold off on this week.

Start 'Em Quarterbacks in Week 4 of 2026 NFL Season

If you haven't been starting Shough since the end of the 2025 season, you're already missing out. The New Orleans Saints quarterback has been one of the best-performing quarterbacks through the first three weeks of the season, and he's not slowing down anytime soon. Shough went for 255 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders for 24.2 fantasy points.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Shough will be going up against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 4. It's a divisional matchup, but Atlanta's defense has been so-and-so against quarterbacks in fantasy specifically. Shough owners should ride the hot hand and go with the Saints quarterback in Week 4.

Prescott has been one of the better quarterbacks in fantasy this season, averaging around 22 fantasy points through three weeks. Against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 3, he was excellent, throwing for 276 yards and one touchdown for 18.9 fantasy points. One of the more turnover-prone quarterbacks in the league, Prescott has done an excellent job this season limiting his turnovers.

A matchup against the Houston Texans should scare managers on paper, given the team's reputation as one of the best defensive units in the league. However, their passing defense has been surprisingly suspect to start the year. They've given up the eighth-most points to quarterbacks through three weeks. With their passing defense in a bit of a slump as of late, you can count on Prescott to help out your fantasy team.

Brock Purdy's ascension through the NFL ranks has been fascinating to watch. Even with a depleted wide receiver room, the 49ers quarterback is still playing the best football of his career. He's coming off two starts of 28+ fantasy points, the latest of which was a 31.3 FPTS outing in Week 3 where he threw for nearly 300 yards and four touchdowns without a single turnover.

Purdy will take on a tough Denver Broncos defense, yes. But Denver has been middle-of-the-pack in terms of fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks, and a favorable game-state should force the 49ers to throw the ball more.

Sit 'Em Quarterbacks in Week 4 of 2026 NFL Season

Oh, how far Drake Maye has fallen. After an MVP-level campaign in 2025, Maye has severely struggled through the first three weeks of the season. The Patriots quarterback has seven turnovers through three games, most of which were interceptions. Against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3, he threw up a dud, throwing two interceptions, fumbling once, and throwing no touchdowns.

The Buffalo Bills' defense started off slow, but they're starting to show their teeth with a few standout performances. Until Maye can prove that he's shaken off whatever's affecting his play, he's not worth a starting spot in any fantasy league.

The Chargers' Mike McDaniel-Justin Herbert experiment has not worked out well. In fact, it's been absolutely dreadful. The Chargers offense looks like one of the worst units in the league this season, and Herbert's struggles are part of the issue. He's thrown an interception in each of his first three games, and has just averaged 12.6 points to start the year.

A matchup against the in-form Seattle Seahawks defense should make things even worse for Herbert. Like with Maybe, Herbert has to prove that his mojo is back first before being entrusted with a starting role in fantasy leagues again.

Kirk Cousins has shown impeccable form through the first three games of the season. He's been remarkably consistent to start the year, finishing with more than 15 fantasy points in each of the first three weeks of the season. He's coming off an incredible performance against the Saints, throwing for 248 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions.

Unfortunately, Cousins and the Raiders are running into a buzzsaw named the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs defense has allowed the fewest points to quarterbacks in fantasy this season. While Cousins' strong start is a great feel-good story to start the year, there's nothing to indicate that he can overcome one of the stingiest defensive units in the league.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

In Week 3, Washington logged five carries for 54 yards and a touchdown.

Robinson caught seven of 11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown last Sunday.

There's obviously no guarantee that Robinson will be as heavily targeted this week, but he should be a big part of the game plan. The Titans will likely pass early and often while trying to keep pace with the Baltimore Ravens.

articles.body:
The first month of the 2026 NFL season is done, and Bleacher Report's expert crew is ready to turn the page to the October slate.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford had a rough September, but it's a long season, which leaves plenty of time for adjustments as the panel gets a handle on this year's trends.

This week, most of the experts favor big spreads and road favorites, with one unanimous pick. They're only siding with one of the five 0-3 teams against the spread.

Looking at the standings below, there's some ground to make up, but with a strong start to October, our crew can get on the right track for a midseason run.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 30, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) at Cleveland Browns (2-1)

Maybe this is the jaded Steelers fan talking, but this just feels like a classic Steelers loss. Perhaps those are a thing of the bygone Mike Tomlin era, but we'll see.

Pittsburgh secured a huge win over the Bengals last week, but going into Cleveland on a short week against a Browns team growing in confidence can be a tall order.

Since 2019, the Browns are 6-1 at home against the Steelers. Behind an inspired defensive effort, I like Cleveland to win this one and somehow be the 3-1 leaders of the AFC North coming out of the game.

After three weeks, it is hard to know whether either 2-1 team is actually any good. Spencer Fano has played like a rookie, Tytus Howard has been a liability, Elgton Jenkins is injured, and Deshaun Watson has typically struggled under pressure as Cleveland's quarterback.

Contrary to what Todd Monken may wish , T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward are not retiring before Thursday night. They will force Watson into the sort of mistakes that lead to a Cleveland loss and have Browns fans calling for Shedeur Sanders before the end of the night.

Steelers: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton

Indianapolis Colts (1-2) vs. Washington Commanders (1-2)

I'm not giving up a hook with the Colts outside of Indianapolis, especially considering how Washington fared against Seattle in Week 3. Indy beat Houston at home last week, but that 19-17 victory was just about the ugliest win you can earn. I expect Washington's run game to control this game, leading to a Commanders victory.

Here's the quandary: Both the Colts and Commanders produced impressive victories last weekend after 0-2 starts, yet it's difficult to believe in either of them.

Indianapolis gets the nod, because it's not relying on a backup quarterback to keep the team afloat. Meanwhile, Daniel Jones will be facing the league's second-worst pass defense, which should signal big days from Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren.

Colts: Davenport, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Tennessee Titans (0-3) at Baltimore Ravens (2-1)

The Titans' last two losses have come by a total of nine points, while the Ravens have been outscored by four in their last two games combined.

Baltimore is at home here, but those two "meh" performances didn't come on the road, either. Now it's coming off an energy-zapping trip to Brazil.

This might not be a complete trap that results in a shocking loss, but I'm not giving up double-digit points.

Typically, it's wise to take the points with massive spreads, but the Titans offense isn't even good enough for a back-door cover. Meanwhile, the Ravens field the fourth-ranked scoring offense.

This will also be Derrick Henry's first time facing his former team, and he's the focal point of the Ravens' high-scoring attack. Baltimore won't have to do much to slow down the Titans' sparkless offense. Ravens roll by at least two touchdowns.

Ravens: Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Green Bay Packers (1-2) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3)

Going down to Tampa and losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback would have felt like a very Packers thing to do in past years. I don't think this Packers team is as good as those we've seen in recent years, either.

Green Bay has gone 1-7 since losing Micah Parsons to a torn ACL last season, and its one win came in overtime against the Jets. I think if the Packers manage to win this one, it won't be by much.

The Buccaneers scored fewer than 20 points in their last two games with Baker Mayfield under center. So, it's hard to believe they'll flip the offensive switch with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at the helm.

The Packers had extra time to think about an embarrassing home-opening loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers' 23rd-ranked rushing attack won't bludgeon the Packers' defensive front like Bijan Robinson did last Thursday. Packers bounce back big against a winless team with a quarterback making his first start.

Packers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) at Cincinnati Bengals (2-1)

The Bengals are finally back home after two weeks on the road and coming off a tough Week 3 loss.

The Jaguars have been great overall, led by a daunting defense, but I like Joe Burrow and Cincinnati to test them way more than the Patriots did last week.

The Jaguars bounced back in Week 3 after a disappointing defeat to the Denver Broncos. Cincinnati will look to do the same after falling to the rival Pittsburgh Steelers.

However, the Bengals remain mistake-prone, as quarterback Joe Burrow stated after the loss . Cincinnati is the league's sixth-most penalized team . Conversely, Jacksonville is tied for the fewest penalties through three weeks, which gives the Jaguars an edge while also taking the points.

Jaguars: Davenport, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Los Angeles Rams (1-2) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-1)

There's nothing to feel good about in picking this one.

The Eagles are licking their wounds after a Monday Night Football beatdown by journeyman QB Case Keenum and a Chicago Bears defense ripe for exploitation; the Eagles scored only seven, very questionable at best, points in the game. They're a 2-1 team that feels like it's 0-3.

The vaunted, super-duper-Hollywood Rams are 1-2 and feel like they should be 0-3, too. After blowing a 16-point lead in Denver, and injuries aside, Sean McVay's team desperately needs to find itself.

This game will probably be a push, but I have to make a pick, and I'll back the more desperate team since it has actually shown some ability to score points this season.

So, everyone else is picking the Rams. Don't count these Eagles out. Despite Philadelphia looking like the bad version from last season while playing the Case Keenum-led Bears, Nick Sirianni's group knows how to respond. The team has gone through stretches of stagnation before and tended to bounce back.

Plus, the idea of this Rams team isn't quite as good as everyone expected should be discussed. The embarrassing loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia can be forgotten due to poor travel plans. But Sunday's second-half loss after holding a 16-0 halftime lead is inexcusable. Furthermore, Matthew Stafford isn't playing at an MVP level anymore.

Rams: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

New England Patriots (1-2) at Buffalo Bills (3-0)

This game features two teams barreling in opposite directions. The Bills have issues on defense, but the offense has been a buzzsaw. The Patriots have issues all over the place, and quarterback Drake Maye has looked overwhelmed.

New England hasn't scored more than 20 points this season and is averaging 12 points per game. Bills by double digits at home.

New England's offense has been a mess, but the Patriots and Bills played two very close games last season, and there is still plenty of talent and experience here.

The Patriots are in a desperate spot and should be expected to again put up a fight against their division rival. The Bills looked out of sorts against the Chargers, and only one of their three wins has come in remotely convincing fashion. This feels like a field-goal game.

Bills: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski

New York Jets (1-2) at Chicago Bears (2-1)

The Bears looked fantastic in Monday night's demolition of the Philadelphia Eagles, but the hook is a bridge too far for me here. The Jets have been decent offensively with Geno Smith in his second stint with the team, and he'll keep this a close one. Chicago will get the win in a close one, but Gang Green will get the cover.

Tyson Bagent should be back under center, which bodes well for a Chicago team that dominated the Eagles with Case Keenum running the show. The Jets have been more competitive than expected so far thanks to Geno Smith's solid play at QB, but their second straight road game takes its toll here. The Bears keep things rolling and move to 3-1 as they're one week closer to Caleb Williams' return.

Arizona Cardinals (1-2) at New York Giants (2-1)

The Giants will feel the absence of Brian Burns on defense, but I still have confidence that this is a unit that can make this game ugly enough to get a win. The Cardinals are 11-23 on the East Coast in the last two seasons. They're a team prone to games that don't always make sense and backdoor covers, but I like the Giants to make this one ugly and win by a field goal.

The John Harbaugh Giants, sans Jaxson Dart and now sans Brian Burns, are impossible to get a read on at this point. The team that won in Week 1 no longer exists. Dart (and Nabers) were injured in the Week 2 game—that team and game basically don't count. The victorious Week 3 team played a hapless Titans squad featuring too many former Giants for anyone's liking in a rain-soaked, wind-rattled mess of a game.

The Jameis Winston experience is always an adventure, but we're truly in uncharted territory here. The Cardinals tend to hang around in games and/or storm back in garbage time, and I struggle to see any version of the Giants putting a team away right now. So, even in a virtual pick 'em, I'll take the points.

Cardinals: Davenport, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Dallas Cowboys (1-2) at Houston Texans (0-3)

After yet another 0-3 start, it's desperation time in Houston—and a potential turning point in the career of Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud.

The problem for Houston is that the Dallas offense can move the ball against just about anyone, and I just don't trust the Texans to be able to score enough points.

Houston is headed for an 0-4 start, and the criticism of Stroud's play is about to become much louder.

The Texans must win now, or they can probably forget about the playoffs. Only the 1992 San Diego Chargers have started the season 0-4 and made the postseason. The Texans have bounced back from 0-3 starts to clinch playoff berths, but they shouldn't test a more unfavorable history.

In an early win-now situation, the Texans finally respond against one of the league's worst defenses. The Cowboys should be embarrassed by their loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro last week, but that shame won't fix the holes in their defense or their subpar defensive play-calling. Also, it would be a quick turnaround for newly acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

Wide receiver Nico Collins, who practiced on Wednesday, returns to propel the Texans to a season-saving win.

Texans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Miami Dolphins (0-3) at Minnesota Vikings (3-0)

To be clear, this has nothing to do with the Dolphins, who have struggled badly through three weeks and could be headed for a difficult season—especially with De'Von Achane reportedly out for the year.

Still, the spread is large for a Minnesota offense that has been inconsistent and could be without Justin Jefferson.

The Vikings should win comfortably, but a late Miami touchdown could produce a back-door cover.

The Dolphins aren't competitive. They've lost all three of their games by at least 14 points, and their best offensive skill player, De'Von Achane, is out for the season with a torn ACL.

Even if Justin Jefferson sits out or plays at less than 100 percent, Minnesota's second-ranked scoring defense may allow no more than a touchdown and a couple of field goals. Kyler Murray will have his best game as a Viking in an 11-plus-point blowout win.

Vikings: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Los Angeles Chargers (0-3) at Seattle Seahawks (2-1)

Something is extremely off with this Chargers team, and now they're in the wrong place at the wrong time, with Seattle back at home following a tough loss to Washington. Mike Macdonald's defense is due for a big playmaking affair against an untrustworthy Justin Herbert. This could be a blowout.

This is less about the Chargers being good and more about the idea that they can't be this bad. Mike McDaniel's offense has been a disaster, but the Seahawks defense showed some cracks against Washington last week. If this spread was smaller, I'd back Seattle coming off an upset loss. But this is enough points where I see Justin Herbert keeping things just close enough.

Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Denver Broncos (2-1) at San Francisco 49ers (3-0)

You would think I'd know better than to go against Brock Purdy, but I'm an idiot, so there. Denver's 2-1 record despite slow starts and a brutal schedule speaks to the talent on its roster.

With Mike Evans joining San Francisco's lengthy injury list, this could be the week the 49ers' mounting absences finally catch up with them.

This feels like a trap to me, but I'm going to ignore it.

The Broncos are a solid team—good, though not great—that can win in a variety of ways. It's almost never pretty, but it has proved effective. While many keep waiting for San Francisco's injuries to catch up with the Purdy-led 49ers, I'm not biting.

Purdy is really good whether you want to believe it or not. He's good whether the 49ers are healthy (which is never) or not. Laying less than a field goal at home, I'm going to ignore my instinct to take the points thinking the unbeaten 'Niners aren't real because I believe they are very much for real right now.

Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-0)

The Las Vegas Raiders are light-years better than they've been over the past few years. So, this could be a competitive matchup, especially with head coach Klint Kubiak maximizing Brock Bowers' skill set in the passing game.

However, during the preseason, the Raiders' run defense was their biggest issue. And over the last two weeks, Las Vegas has allowed over 126 rushing yards to a Los Angeles Chargers offense without an identity and a pass-heavy New Orleans Saints squad.

Now, the Raiders have to stop league-leading rusher Kenneth Walker III, who's averaging 120 yards on the ground per game. Kansas City won't turn the ball over four consecutive drives like New Orleans did last week. The Chiefs have two turnovers in three weeks. Without takeaways, and with the threat of Kansas City's newfound ground game, the Raiders fall by at least a touchdown.

This selection is less about believing in the 3-0 Raiders and more about how they can attack the rival Chiefs. With Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye working off the edges, the tandem can terrorize the Chiefs offense due to Kansas City's weakness at offensive tackle.

Plus, those two can help slow Kenneth Walker, and make Kansas City's offense less potent than it's been so far. If Kirk Cousins continues to play smart football, he doesn't need to outperform Patrick Mahomes. Instead, the Raiders quarterback can keep his squad on schedule and show they're not to be overlooked any longer.

Chiefs: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

Detroit Lions (2-1) at Carolina Panthers (1-2)

With rain in the forecast, I do have concerns about the conditions potentially limiting the two talented offenses in this matchup. It doesn't look like any of us are backing Carolina, but it's not outlandish to think the Panthers can keep it close in a sloppy, mistake-filled game at home.

That said, I don't expect to see a lot of great defense, and I expect a fairly high-scoring game. With Panthers cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both headed to injured reserve, the Lions should have an opportunity to open things up and pull away late.

Detroit doesn't deserve my trust, but that's why I'm going to back them.

The Lions' offense simply isn't as scary as it could be. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown rack up the numbers, but the offensive output isn't dominating enough to cover for a banged-up defense that can't keep teams more than one score away from taking a lead and/or stealing a win.

Carolina is getting the best out of Bryce Young, but unless it's defending against Cooper Rush, the Panthers' defense can be taken to the woodshed.

Let's queue up a likely shootout that ends with Carolina needing a touchdown to tie/win late, not getting it, and giving the Lions their first ATS cover of the season.

Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Atlanta Falcons (1-2) at New Orleans Saints (1-2)

The Atlanta Falcons' offense was stunningly effective in Michael Penix Jr.'s 2026 debut last Thursday. However, I'm not convinced we'll see Penix play with such efficiency for a second straight week—not in New Orleans on a night honoring the 20th anniversary of the "Domecoming" game.

The Saints' offense may be a bit one-dimensional with Travis Etienne Jr. sidelined, but I think we'll see New Orleans' defense, the home crowd, and Tyler Shough take over the game and deliver at least a three-point victory.

The Falcons had their big, surprise performance of the year last week when they beat the Packers at Lambeau Field. It's a struggle to think they can string together strong back-to-back performances, especially against a division rival that seems poised to turn the corner sooner rather than later.

But the Falcons are 5-1 ATS as road 'dogs since the start of last season, a mark good enough for fourth-best in the league. Even if they don't get a second straight victory, I'll settle for a potential cover against a Saints team that seems to really fancy playing close games.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 4 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: As we enter Week 4, many fantasy managers have concerns about their quarterback situation. Drake Maye and Justin Herbert are struggling mightily. Jaxson Dart is out for the season. Jayden Daniels and Baker Mayfield are on short-term injured reserve. It's time to invest in a QB2.
articles.body:
As we enter Week 4, many fantasy managers have concerns about their quarterback situation. Drake Maye and Justin Herbert are struggling mightily. Jaxson Dart is out for the season. Jayden Daniels and Baker Mayfield are on short-term injured reserve. It's time to invest in a QB2.

This week's sleepers list features a known quarterback commodity in a favorable matchup and an undrafted rookie set to make his first start. Both can help you through concerns about starting Maye or Herbert.

We'll also see teams shuffle backfields with new lead running backs or redistribute touches. If you miss out on New York Jets tailback Braelon Allen, who's set to fill in for the injured Breece Hall, there are decent alternatives.

You'll need to wake up for a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff in London to track one of our wide receiver sleepers, but he's worth starting in an early slot. Lastly, a tight end makes his second appearance on the sleeper list in a smash spot.

Here are the biggest sleepers at every position—all of them are available in more than 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros .

QB Jacoby Brissett at New York Giants (11 Percent Rostered)

The Arizona Cardinals have shown more offensive upside than their overall record may suggest.

They field a respectable offense, scoring 26 and 30 points in two road matchups against the Los Angeles Chargers and San Francisco 49ers, respectively.

Aside from a home matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, who have allowed the third-fewest points and fewest yards, the Cardinals can score in flurries. They'll face the New York Giants, who rank 19th in passing yards allowed and have given up seven touchdowns through the air.

Last week, Jacoby Brissett finished as QB4 in fantasy scoring, throwing for 280 yards and two touchdowns against the 49ers. Arizona fell behind early, so he had to be aggressive. That said, with tight end Trey McBride and wideout Michael Wilson as his top targets, Brissett can find success in the passing game against the Giants' inconsistent coverage.

If you're a manager hesitant to start Drake Maye or prepared to cut Justin Herbert, add Brissett for Week 4.

QB Jalon Daniels vs. Green Bay Packers (1 Percent Rostered)

Jalon Daniels is a true fantasy dart throw. An undrafted rookie out of Kansas, he's set to make his first pro start in place of Baker Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb last week.

In Week 3, Daniels didn't complete any of his three pass attempts, but after a full week of practice with the starters, he'll be better prepared for action. Because of his dual-threat playmaking ability, the athletic signal-caller has intriguing upside.

Over six collegiate seasons, Daniels threw for 9,282 yards, 67 touchdowns, and 31 interceptions, and ran for 1,445 yards and 23 scores. He will have a solid receiver unit featuring 2025 first-rounder Emeka Egbuka, savvy 10-year veteran Chris Godwin and Ted Hurst III, who scored his first NFL touchdown last week.

With that pass-catching group, Daniels could rack up yards against the Green Bay Packers, who are tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers. If he struggles to establish rhythm in rainy conditions, expect him to use his legs.

RB Ollie Gordon II at Minnesota Vikings (26 Percent Rostered)

De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL, so if you're a manager in need of running back help, pick a Miami Dolphins running back between Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright. Both tailbacks should see an uptick in touches.

At 6'2", 225 pounds, Gordon will likely handle short-yardage and goal-line touches, which makes him the preferred option over Wright, who's a smaller ball-carrier at 5'10", 205 pounds.

Moreover, Wright missed last week's game because of a stinger and a foot injury. So, even if he suits up on Sunday, he may not handle a full workload.

The Dolphins may have limited scoring opportunities against the Minnesota Vikings' second-ranked scoring defense, but Gordon's expanded role will allow him chances to sneak into the end zone.

RB Kendre Miller vs. Atlanta Falcons (4 Percent Rostered)

Late in last Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders, running back Travis Etienne Jr. aggravated a hamstring injury that recently limited him at practices. Head coach Kellen Moore told reporters there will be " time lost " for the Saints' lead ball-carrier.

Last week, Alvin Kamara made the sleeper list . He'll be hard to find in free-agent pools for Week 4, so turn your attention to his running mate, Kendre Miller.

In his prime, Kamara was more effective in space rather than running between the tackles and took on a lighter rushing workload than most lead ball-carriers. Don't expect him to handle 20-plus carries regularly in his age-31 season.

If healthy, Miller should handle plenty of touches out of the backfield. With Kamara sidelined by an MCL sprain in Week 1, Miller shared the backfield with Etienne and recorded nine carries for 30 yards and a touchdown.

The Saints have a bottom-six rushing offense, but Miller could log 10-plus carries and see a few targets Monday night.

WR Keenan Allen vs. Washington Commanders (27 Percent Rostered)

Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has recorded six receptions in two out of three games—one with Alec Pierce and one without him. He's third on the team in receptions (13) and second in receiving yards (100).

Pierce will miss at least three more games on injured reserve, so it's a good time to pick up Allen, who's familiar with play-calling head coach Shane Steichen's offense from their time with the Los Angeles Chargers. In Steichen's system, Allen played at a Pro Bowl level several years ago.

At 34, Allen is much older in his reunion with Steichen, but he's the Colts' No. 2 receiver in a matchup against the Washington Commanders' 31st-ranked pass defense. By the way, Washington allowed the Seattle Seahawks to accumulate 393 passing yards in Sam Darnold's first game back from a two-week injury absence.

Even at his age, Allen has flex appeal in a game with a high-end scoring total line of 47.5 on FanDuel .

WR Kalif Raymond vs. New York Jets (19 Percent Rostered)

Initially, Kalif Raymond's production seemed fluky because the Chicago Bears have wideouts Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze and tight end Colston Loveland. However, after seeing at least five targets in all three games, he's established a stable role in the offense.

In fact, Raymond leads the Bears in catches (19) and receiving yards (214), going into Week 4. He only has two fewer targets than Burden.

As the Bears' lead pass-catcher in multiple receiving categories, Raymond should be rostered in far more leagues. Even with 38-year-old Case Keenum under center, he caught six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown last Monday night.

Keenum isn't a lock to start Sunday, but the Bears draw a decent matchup against the New York Jets, who have allowed two passing touchdowns in consecutive weeks. Assuming Raymond continues to see a steady share of targets, he's a viable WR3/flex option.

TE Darren Waller vs. Detroit Lions (21 Percent Rostered)

Detroit has allowed the most passing yards in the NFL, and Carolina's injuries at wide receiver could increase Darren Waller's target outlook. He is in a strong Week 4 spot.

The Lions' banged-up defense, without its starting safeties, allows the most fantasy points to tight ends . Detroit has surrendered a touchdown to six different tight ends—two in each of its games this season.

Panthers wideout Jalen Coker is questionable to play because of a quad injury, and Xavier Legette missed last week's game due to a knee issue. Even if one or both receivers suit up, expect Carolina to feature Waller in a potential high-scoring matchup. FanDuel has set the scoring total line at 50.5 points.

TE AJ Barner vs. Los Angeles Chargers (14 Percent Rostered)

With Sam Darnold returning from a glute injury, AJ Barner was more involved in the passing game than in the first two weeks of the season.

After hauling in all three of his targets for 21 yards in a Drew Lock-led offense, he caught five of nine targets for 69 yards from Darnold last week.

Last season, Barner ranked second on the Seahawks in targets and receptions and third in receiving yards and touchdown catches, finishing with 68 targets, 52 receptions, 519 yards and six scores. With Darnold under center, he has maintained a consistent role in Seattle's passing attack.

On Sunday, the Seahawks will host a winless Los Angeles Chargers squad that ranks 21st in passing yards allowed and 26th in net yards allowed per pass attempt.

While star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba commands most of the attention downfield, Barner can take advantage of soft coverage in the short-to-intermediate zones.

Fantasy points scored against statistics are provided by FantasyPros .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Drake Maye, Mike McDaniel and the NFL's Biggest Disappointments of 2026 So Far
articles.summary: We're only three weeks into the 2026 NFL season, but it's safe to say that things haven't unfolded quite the way most expected.
articles.body:
We're only three weeks into the 2026 NFL season, but it's safe to say that things haven't unfolded quite the way most expected.

The reigning AFC champion New England Patriots, for example, are sitting at 1-2. So are the Los Angeles Rams, who reached last year's NFC title game and were the heavily hyped preseason Super Bowl favorites. Other teams we expected to push for the playoffs, such as the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans, are still winless entering Week 4.

There have been some pleasant surprises in 2026, too, like the undefeated Las Vegas Raiders.

However, we're here to focus on the biggest disappointments of the season so far. We'll examine who has fallen furthest short of expectations, why, and what may come next.

Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers' Offense

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had their streak of four straight NFC South titles snapped last season. However, there was some belief that with a healthier roster and a new offensive coordinator in Zac Robinson, they could rebound in 2026.

That's undoubtedly part of the reason why Tampa gave quarterback Baker Mayfield a new three-year, $165 million extension just before the start of the season.

Unfortunately, things have not gone according to plan. The Buccaneers' offense hasn't found a legitimate replacement for departed star receiver Mike Evans, and Mayfield was mistake-prone through the first three weeks of the season—and he's now set to miss time with a dislocated thumb .

Mayfield has thrown just two touchdown passes, committed five turnovers, and has a passer rating of just 80.0. While he's out, the Bucs will turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels.

While fans can certainly hope Daniels can provide a spark to the offense, Mayfield hasn't been the only issue. Robinson's predictable play-calling has made it difficult to sustain drives and establish a rhythm.

Tampa's sixth-ranked defense has been good enough to keep the Buccaneers in games, but the Bucs are sitting at 0-3 because their offense has been flat-out bad to this point. If things don't change quickly, Tampa will land in the NFC South basement and may have to consider sweeping changes in the offseason.

While some may have expected a regression from the Buccaneers offense this season, virtually no one anticipated Drake Maye falling flat on his face after being last year's MVP runner-up.

Maye hasn't just regressed this season; he has become a significant concern for the Patriots.

The third-year quarterback's three-interception performance in Week 1 included a costly end-zone interception on New England's final, potentially game-winning drive. He has yet to show a sustained rebound since that opener.

Through three weeks, Maye has completed just 63.8 percent of his passes for 585 yards, one touchdown, six interceptions, and a dreadful 58.6 passer rating. He has also fumbled twice, losing one.

Speculation about the signal-caller's standing has intensified after WEEI host Greg Hill suggested head coach Mike Vrabel may not view him as his preferred quarterback.

"Despite what Mike Vrabel has said publicly, it goes back to Drake Maye not being his guy," Hill said on The Greg Hill Show .

Vrabel has since publicly downplayed the idea that Maye isn't his guy. However, support from his head coach isn't going to magically fix his play on the field.

So why has Maye taken such a big step backward? Well, for one thing, he's faced a tough early schedule after playing one of the NFL's easiest in 2025. He's also been without his go-to receiver since A.J. Brown exited with an ankle injury in Week 1.

The reality is that Maye's Year 2 jump may not have been as massive as it might seem at first glance—and his shaky play against quality opponents in the playoffs supports that idea. He still has a lot of room for growth, and he should make some positive strides as the season progresses.

Of course, if Maye cannot do a better job of protecting the football, New England will struggle to get back to the postseason.

The Los Angeles Chargers made the playoffs in each of the past two seasons, due largely to the strength of their defense. Quarterback Justin Herbert regularly did enough to make L.A.'s offense functional, but a lack of offensive efficiency and creativity led to the firing of offensive coordinator Greg Roman.

Following the dismissal of Roman, the Chargers scooped up former San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator and former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel.

Having developed a reputation as one of the NFL's brightest young offensive minds, McDaniel was expected to significantly boost the Chargers offense while fully unlocking Herbert as a signal-caller. Instead, both Herbert and the Chargers' offense have gotten worse.

Los Angeles ranks just 29th in scoring, while Herbert holds a passer rating (73.4) that is more than 20 points below his career average (95.8). The Chargers' defense has also seemingly regressed, but the sudden fall of Herbert, long considered an upper-tier starter, has been stunning.

McDaniel has already come under fire to a degree that head coach Jim Harbaugh felt the need to publicly defend his OC following L.A.'s latest loss.

"No, we trust Mike. We believe in Mike," Harbaugh said, per Austin Knoblauch of the Los Angeles Times .

The Chargers may believe in McDaniel, but if they don't start getting better results out of the offense, and Herbert, in particular, there's virtually no way that they'll reach the postseason for the third straight year.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

The Rams' Duo of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett

This one has been a massive disappointment simply because we haven't seen it yet.

The Rams shocked the football world a couple of times during the offseason. First, they made a blockbuster trade for pass-rusher and reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in June. Then, they announced the un-retirement of three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald.

The two future Hall of Famers were supposed to anchor an elite defensive front on a championship-caliber defense that also added cornerbacks Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie in the offseason.

However, Donald didn't travel with the Rams to Australia for the opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Despite being on the field, Garrett was just as productive as Donald in Week 1, which he finished with no tackles, sacks, or QB pressures. We quickly learned that Garrett was dealing with a significant knee injury, one that required surgery and a move to injured reserve.

According to ESPN's Ian Rapoport , Garrett is looking at a six-week recovery timeline.

Donald has appeared in Los Angeles' last two games and has played like he didn't spend the last two years in retirement. He has four tackles, one tackle for loss, and one quarterback pressure while playing 54 percent of the defensive snaps.

At some point, Garrett should be healthy enough to return to the field, and if he's even close to his 2024 form, he and Donald can be the terrifying tandem most expected them to be. However, it's going to be several more weeks before that happens.

In the meantime, the Rams must start stringing together wins, or else Garrett's return might not really matter.

Last offseason, the Tennessee Titans made former Miami quarterback Cam Ward the No. 1 overall pick in the draft. He was named the starter ahead of Week 1, and he started all 17 games as a rookie.

While Ward showed some flashes of elite upside during his inaugural campaign, his production (3,169 yards, 15 TDs, 7 INTs, 80.2 QB rating) was very underwhelming overall. Of course, he was saddled with one of the league's most underwhelming supporting casts.

That's why it wasn't hard to envision a big second-year jump from Ward. Tennessee hired a new head coach in Robert Saleh and an experienced offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll this past offseason.

The Titans then added new offensive pieces such as center Austin Schlottmann, receiver Wan'Dale Robinson, tight end Daniel Bellinger and rookie wideout Carnell Tate .

Unfortunately, the substantial growth many expected to see from Ward hasn't come. He's thrown for just 504 yards with two touchdowns, an interception, and an 80.9 QB rating through three weeks. His lack of development is a big reason why Tennessee sits at 0-3 with the league's 31st-ranked offense.

According to Saleh, Ward's poor start to 2026 may be an aftereffect of his rookie season.

"You've got to remember the young man was sacked however many times last year so I'm sure there's some PTSD there," Saleh told reporters . "But he's getting better. He's trusting it. His footwork is lasting him longer into games if that makes sense."

Regardless of why Ward's growth has been stunted, his lack of progress has been glaring in contrast to Tyler Shough's second-year strides.

If the former Hurricanes star doesn't start playing much better, much more consistently, and very soon, the Titans could face difficult questions about Ward's long-term development.

With the 2027 draft class expected to be deep with quarterback talent, a lack of Year-2 progress from Ward could leave Tennessee with some very difficult decisions in the spring.

This one's for the fantasy enthusiasts who drafted Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland early, believing him to be a potential league-winner.

A year ago, he appeared to be on the doorstep of the NFL's elite tight end club. The Michigan product finished his inaugural NFL campaign with 58 catches for 713 yards and six touchdowns.

With wide receiver D.J. Moore being traded in the spring, it certainly felt like Loveland's ceiling could be even higher this season.

Through three games, though, Loveland has caught just five of nine targets for 34 yards. He did appear to have a touchdown reception on Monday night, but he was ruled short after review.

Fans may be wondering if there's something ailing Loveland or if he has simply fallen out of favor following the offseason departure of offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. However, the player's meager production has a simpler explanation, as the tight end noted himself.

"There's other ways to make plays on the ground in the run game," Loveland said, per Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic. "I'm just doing what I'm asked and … there's going to be opportunities."

Loveland didn't catch either of his Week 1 targets, and Chicago's offense sputtered after losing Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury in Week 2. Last week, Case Keenum had the offense clicking again, and Loveland caught a season-high four passes on four targets.

After playing just 65 percent of the offensive snaps as a rookie, Loveland has played 84 percent of the snaps through Week 3. However, it's unlikely that his underwhelming statistics will be a season-long trend.

The Texans made the playoffs for the third consecutive year in 2025, thanks in large part to their elite defense.

While quarterback C.J. Stroud and the Texans' offense had their fair share of issues last season, Houston regularly relied on a defense that ranked first overall and second in points allowed. The unit included three Pro Bowlers in linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. and edge-rusher Will Anderson Jr.

Most expected that Houston's defense would again be championship-caliber in 2026, and that with a little offensive improvement, the Texans might even emerge as Super Bowl contenders. However, that hasn't happened.

Stroud and the offense actually looked quite potent in the season opener, a 36-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills. That side of the ball hasn't been as dependable over the last two games, contests that star receiver Nico Collins missed with a hamstring injury. However, the Texans' defense really hasn't been dependable at all this season.

Through three weeks, Houston ranks 26th in passing yards allowed, 16th in total yards allowed, and 19th in points allowed. The Texans enter Week 4 still searching for their first win largely because their defense has failed them, a fact that was probably not on anyone's 2026 NFL bingo card.

Now, it's worth noting that Houston overcame a 0-3 start last year and still made the playoffs. However, the Texans will have to do a better job of limiting big plays in the passing game while forcing turnovers if they're going to get back to the sort of defensive football that has made them a postseason threat over the last three seasons.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 4 Top 50 NFL Players' Updated Trade Value and Advice
articles.summary: By the time we hit Week 4 of the fantasy football season, trends are starting to emerge. While plenty can change beyond the first month of the NFL season, a better idea of what your team is shaping up to be has emerged.
articles.body:
By the time we hit Week 4 of the fantasy football season, trends are starting to emerge. While plenty can change beyond the first month of the NFL season, a better idea of what your team is shaping up to be has emerged.

If have holes to fill and don't want to rely on the waiver wire providing options to address them, it's time to hit the trade block. And in an effort to ensure you don't get ripped off, we've provided the 50 players in fantasy football with the most trade value this season.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

In Parker Washington's last seven games (including the Wild Card loss to the Buffalo Bills last season), he has 41 receptions for 568 yards and five touchdowns. In PPR leagues, that's 18.2 points per game. Over the course of a 17-game season, that production translates to 99 receptions for 1,379 yards and 12 touchdowns.

That, ladies and gentleman, is absolutely elite production. You may have questions about whether he can enter the absolute upper echelon at the position, and that's fair. But a seven-game sample size is pretty telling, and Washington is emerging as one of fantasy's more reliable wideouts. If you can somehow buy low on him now, it may be your final chance.

Is this the year that Christian Watson goes from a streaky fantasy player completely reliant on splash plays to a consistent player you can trust on a weekly basis?

It's still a bit hard to say, given that 34 percent of his fantasy value thus far this season has come from four touchdowns. But what is extremely promising is that he's been targeted 29 times (tied for sixth in the NFL among wideouts) and has turned that into 17 receptions for 284 yards and the aforementioned four touchdowns. He leads the Packers in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns and is second in targets by just one behind Matthew Golden (30).

Watson's past volatility, his injury history and his unsustainable touchdown pace still leaves him more of a sell-high option than a buy-low target at this point. But given that he's currently WR5 in all of fantasy football, make sure you are selling very high—chances are he's still going to be a top-20 player at the position if he stays healthy, even as the touchdown pace inevitably normalizes.

articles.title: A top QB showdown and a historic anniversary: 5 things to know from the NFL this week
articles.summary: Three weeks into the NFL season, we’re already seeing some familiar storylines, some huge surprises and plenty of history being made.
articles.body: Three weeks into the NFL season, we’re already seeing some familiar storylines, some huge surprises and plenty of history being made. The Houston Texans are 0-3 – again – while the Las Vegas Raiders are sitting at a surprising 3-0. Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence are renewing a rivalry this week that goes all the way back to college; some of the NFL’s biggest stars are putting up ridiculous numbers, and Monday night in New Orleans will mark the anniversary of one of the most memorable games in NFL history. Here are five things to watch in Week 4. Texans are 0-3 … again Well, this is déjà vu for Texans fans. Another 0-3 start. Last season, the Texans became just the seventh team ever to make the playoffs after starting 0-3, and they’ve actually done it twice — in 2025 and 2018. But no team has ever lost its first three games and then made the playoffs in back-to-back seasons. And only one team has ever started 0-4 and made the playoffs. That was the 1992 San Diego Chargers, who started 0-4 but then won 11 of their final 12 games. Do the Texans have that kind of run in them? Well, they would have to start finding a way to block and run the ball, but their upcoming schedule isn’t that difficult. Their next seven games are against the Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans, Jacksonville Jaguars in London, New York Giants, Los Angeles Chargers, Cleveland Browns and then the Indianapolis Colts at home. If Houston can go 5-2 during that stretch and get to 5-5, the Texans would be well on their way to salvaging the season. And with the AFC South just 3-9 collectively, chasing down a division title is certainly not out of the question despite another terrible start. The Raiders are 3-0! On the other side of things, Raider Nation is riding high after yet another thrilling win. The Raiders are 3-0 for the first time since 2021 and are actually the first team ever to start a season 3-0 after drafting a quarterback No. 1 overall. But Fernando Mendoza has had nothing to do with the wins. Instead, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins has found the fountain of youth! Cousins has been fantastic, throwing three touchdowns in each of the Raiders’ first three games. Fans were hoping Cousins would play well after he reunited with Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who was his offensive coordinator with the Minnesota Vikings when Cousins had some of the best seasons of his career. Right now, Cousins is tied with San Francisco 49ers QB Brock Purdy for the most passing touchdowns this season. Now, the Raiders’ wins so far have come against the lowly Miami Dolphins, Chargers and New Orleans Saints, so this 3-0 start may turn out to be a bit of a mirage. But if Las Vegas can beat the 3-0 Kansas City Chiefs at home Sunday, that would be a huge statement win – and give the Raiders their first 4-0 start since 2002. Burrow vs. Lawrence We have a showdown between former No. 1 overall picks Sunday in Cincinnati as Joe Burrow and the Bengals host Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars. This is a game Lawrence will certainly be motivated for because he has never beaten Burrow — even dating back to college. Burrow and LSU beat Lawrence and Clemson in the national championship game in January 2020. Burrow has also beaten Lawrence in both of their head-to-head matchups in the NFL. But if Burrow wants to once again get the better of Lawrence, he’d better already be winning late. Burrow is 1-34 when trailing in the final eight minutes of regulation. Just a wild stat. Stars keep scoring If you drafted Jahmyr Gibbs, Jaxon Smith-Njigba or Josh Allen in your fantasy league, you’re likely off to a great start because all three are scoring at a historic pace. Gibbs was the consensus No. 1 overall fantasy pick, and he’s lived up to the hype, scoring six touchdowns in the Detroit Lions’ first three games. He’s just the fifth running back ever to do that to start a season. JSN, meanwhile, has been incredible for the Seahawks, leading the NFL in both receiving yards and touchdowns. He’s had at least 120 receiving yards and a touchdown in each game, joining Hall of Famer Jerry Rice as the only receiver in NFL history to do that in each of the first three games of a season. And then there’s Allen. With two more rushing touchdowns in Sunday’s win over the Chargers, Allen became the first quarterback in NFL history with multiple rushing touchdowns in three consecutive games. The Buffalo QB already has the most rushing touchdowns ever by a quarterback with 85. That puts him tied for 17th on the NFL’s all-time rushing touchdown list. And Allen is still only 30 years old! His Bills will look for a 4-0 start when they host the New England Patriots on Sunday. Katrina anniversary game Monday night will be an emotional one in New Orleans as the Saints commemorate the 20th anniversary of their return to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina. On September 25, 2006, the Saints beat the Atlanta Falcons 23-3 in their first game back at the Superdome following the storm. Steve Gleason’s blocked punt, which was recovered for a Saints touchdown, remains one of the most iconic moments in franchise – and arguably NFL – history. The moment is now immortalized with a statue outside the Superdome. That game became known as the “Domecoming” or “Rebirth” game and served as a powerful symbol of recovery and resilience for the city of New Orleans and the entire Gulf Coast region following the devastation of Hurricane Katrina. Twenty years later, the Falcons and Saints will meet again on Monday night. Both teams enter the matchup at 1-2.
